# Revising GitHub Copilot instructions for monorepo (2025-10-30 03:41Z)

_**User (2025-10-30 14:56Z)**_

Revise the `copilot-instructions.md` to apply to this monorepo. References to Next.js, React, etc should be removed and replaced with Nx and other monorepo-level libraries. Refer to #file:overview.md  and any other `docs/` files as needed. NOTE: individual apps within the `apps/` folder may follow different internal and front-end architectures. (&#96;drawCircle&#96;, &#96;getRandomColor&#96;)\n   - Constants: &#96;UPPER_SNAKE_CASE&#96; (&#96;MAX_PARTICLES&#96;, &#96;DEFAULT_SIZE&#96;)\n4. **p5.js Sketch Structure**: Follow this pattern for p5.js sketches:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n   import { createNamer } from '@genart/p5-utils'\n   import { getPalette } from '@genart/color-palettes'\n   \n   // Configuration and constants\n   const CONFIG = {\n     width: 800,\n     height: 600,\n     backgroundColor: '#ffffff'\n   }\n   \n   // Global variables\n   let namer\n   let palette\n   \n   // p5.js setup function\n   function setup() {\n     createCanvas(CONFIG.width, CONFIG.height)\n     namer = createNamer('my-sketch')\n     palette = getPalette('riso-red-blue')\n     \n     // Additional setup\n   }\n   \n   // p5.js draw function\n   function draw() {\n     background(CONFIG.backgroundColor)\n     // Drawing logic\n   }\n   \n   // Event handlers and utility functions\n   function keyPressed() {\n     if (key === 's') {\n       namer.save()\n     }\n   }\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n5. **Shared Library Usage**: Prefer using shared libraries from &#96;libs/&#96; Nx Monorepo Management\n\n1. **Centralized Commands**: Use Nx commands for consistent development workflow:\n   - &#96;nx dev app-name&#96;: Start development server for specific app\n   - &#96;nx build app-name&#96;: Build specific app for production\n   - &#96;nx run-many --target=dev --all&#96;: Start all apps in development\n   - &#96;nx run-many --target=build --all&#96;: Build all apps\n   - &#96;nx lint app-name&#96;: Lint specific app\n   - &#96;nx test app-name&#96;: Test specific app\n\n2. **Project Configuration**: Each app must have a &#96;project.json&#96; file with proper Nx targets:\n   - &#96;dev&#96;: Development server (typically uses Vite)\n   - &#96;build&#96;: Production build\n   - &#96;lint&#96;: ESLint execution\n   - &#96;test&#96;: Playwright tests (if applicable)\n   - &#96;deploy&#96;: Deployment target (if applicable)\n\n3. **Port Management**: Each app must use a unique development port:\n   - duo-chrome: 5173\n   - crude-collage-painter: 5174\n   - computational-collage: 5175\n   - dragline: 5176\n   - monochromifier: 5177\n   - those-shape-things: 5178\n   - (new projects increment from 5179+)\n\n4. **Dependency Management**: \n   - Use &#96;pnpm&#96; for all package operations\n   - Shared dependencies go in root &#96;package.json&#96;\n   - App-specific dependencies go in app's &#96;package.json&#96;\n   - Shared libraries are consumed via &#96;libs/&#96; workspace references\n\n## 5. Shared Libraries\n\n### @genart/p5-utils\nCommon utilities for p5.js projects:\n- Array manipulation (&#96;getRandomUniqueItem&#96;, &#96;getRandomItem&#96;)\n- File naming (&#96;datestring&#96;, &#96;createFilenamer&#96;)\n- Math utilities (&#96;mapRange&#96;, &#96;constrain&#96;)\n- Canvas utilities and common p5.js patterns\n\n### @genart/color-palettes\nColor management for creative projects:\n- RISO printing colors (authentic ink colors)\n- Custom palette creation and management\n- Color conversion utilities (hex ↔ RGB)\n- Palette sampling and generation\n\n### @genart/version-display\nAutomated version display components:\n- Consistent version display across all apps\n- Automatic version detection and display\n- Customizable styling and positioning\n\n1. **Library Development**: When creating shared functionality:\n   - Identify common patterns across multiple apps\n   - Extract to appropriate library in &#96;libs/&#96;\n   - Update consuming apps to use shared code\n   - Document the library's API and usage\n\n2. **Library Usage**: Always prefer shared libraries over app-specific implementations for common functionality.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n## 6. Individual App Architecture\n\n**Important**: Each app in &#96;apps/&#96; may follow different internal architectures and frameworks. While the end goal is increased code sharing and consistency, projects are allowed to be different to preserve their unique creative approaches.\n\n### Common Patterns Across Apps\n\n1. **Entry Point**: Most apps use &#96;index.html&#96; as the entry point\n2. **Build Tool**: Vite is the standard build tool across all apps\n3. **Source Structure**: Generally follows &#96;src/&#96; for main code, &#96;css/&#96; for styles, &#96;public/&#96; for assets\n4. **Documentation**: Each app maintains its own documentation in &#96;apps/[app-name]/docs/&#96;\n\n### App-Specific Variations\n\n- **Language**: Some apps use JavaScript, others TypeScript\n- **Framework**: Most use vanilla p5.js, but may incorporate other libraries\n- **Structure**: Internal organization varies based on the app's complexity and purpose\n- **Dependencies**: Each app manages its own specific dependencies\n\n### When Working on Apps\n\n1. **Respect Existing Patterns**: When modifying an app, follow its existing conventions\n2. **App Documentation**: Refer to &#96;apps/[app-name]/docs/&#96; for app-specific guidelines\n3. **Gradual Migration**: If proposing architectural changes, plan gradual migrations rather than major rewrites\n4. **Creative Freedom**: Balance consistency with preserving the creative and experimental nature of each project\n\n## 7. Version Management and Releases\n\n1. **Independent Versioning**: Each app maintains its own version using Nx release configuration\n2. **Conventional Commits**: Use conventional commit format to drive automatic version bumps:\n   - &#96;feat:&#96; for new features (minor version bump)\n   - &#96;fix:&#96; for bug fixes (patch version bump)\n   - &#96;feat!:&#96; or &#96;BREAKING CHANGE:&#96; for breaking changes (major version bump)\n3. **Automatic Changelog**: Each app generates its own &#96;CHANGELOG.md&#96; based on commits\n4. **Release Tags**: Git tags follow the pattern &#96;app-name@version&#96; (e.g., &#96;duo-chrome@1.2.0&#96;)\n5. **Release Commands**:\n   - &#96;nx release --projects=app-name&#96;: Release specific app\n   - &#96;nx release&#96;: Release all apps with changes\n\n## 8. Testing Strategy\n\n### Visual Testing with Playwright\n\n1. **End-to-End Testing**: Use Playwright for testing visual applications and user interactions\n2. **Screenshot Testing**: Capture and compare visual outputs for regression testing\n3. **App-Specific Tests**: Each app can have its own test suite in &#96;tests/&#96; or &#96;e2e/&#96;\n4. **Cross-App Testing**: Shared test utilities in &#96;test/&#96; directory\n\n### Test Commands\n\n- &#96;nx test app-name&#96;: Run tests for specific app\n- &#96;nx run-many --target=test --all&#96;: Run all tests\n- &#96;pnpm test:e2e&#96;: Run end-to-end tests\n- &#96;pnpm test:e2e:ui&#96;: Run tests with Playwright UI\n\n### Creative Testing Considerations\n\n- Test interactive features and user controls\n- Verify save/export functionality works correctly\n- Ensure responsive behavior across different screen sizes\n- Test performance with complex generative algorithms\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n",

Nx Monorepo Management\n\n1. **Centralized Commands**: Use Nx commands for consistent development workflow:\n   - &#96;nx dev app-name&#96;: Start development server for specific app\n   - &#96;nx build app-name&#96;: Build specific app for production\n   - &#96;nx run-many --target=dev --all&#96;: Start all apps in development\n   - &#96;nx run-many --target=build --all&#96;: Build all apps\n   - &#96;nx lint app-name&#96;: Lint specific app\n   - &#96;nx test app-name&#96;: Test specific app\n\n2. **Project Configuration**: Each app must have a &#96;project.json&#96; file with proper Nx targets:\n   - &#96;dev&#96;: Development server (typically uses Vite)\n   - &#96;build&#96;: Production build\n   - &#96;lint&#96;: ESLint execution\n   - &#96;test&#96;: Playwright tests (if applicable)\n   - &#96;deploy&#96;: Deployment target (if applicable)\n\n3. **Port Management**: Each app must use a unique development port:\n   - duo-chrome: 5173\n   - crude-collage-painter: 5174\n   - computational-collage: 5175\n   - dragline: 5176\n   - monochromifier: 5177\n   - those-shape-things: 5178\n   - (new projects increment from 5179+)\n\n4. **Dependency Management**: \n   - Use &#96;pnpm&#96; for all package operations\n   - Shared dependencies go in root &#96;package.json&#96;\n   - App-specific dependencies go in app's &#96;package.json&#96;\n   - Shared libraries are consumed via &#96;libs/&#96; workspace references\n\n## 5. Shared Libraries\n\n### @genart/p5-utils\nCommon utilities for p5.js projects:\n- Array manipulation (&#96;getRandomUniqueItem&#96;, &#96;getRandomItem&#96;)\n- File naming (&#96;datestring&#96;, &#96;createFilenamer&#96;)\n- Math utilities (&#96;mapRange&#96;, &#96;constrain&#96;)\n- Canvas utilities and common p5.js patterns\n\n### @genart/color-palettes\nColor management for creative projects:\n- RISO printing colors (authentic ink colors)\n- Custom palette creation and management\n- Color conversion utilities (hex ↔ RGB)\n- Palette sampling and generation\n\n### @genart/version-display\nAutomated version display components:\n- Consistent version display across all apps\n- Automatic version detection and display\n- Customizable styling and positioning\n\n1. **Library Development**: When creating shared functionality:\n   - Identify common patterns across multiple apps\n   - Extract to appropriate library in &#96;libs/&#96;\n   - Update consuming apps to use shared code\n   - Document the library's API and usage\n\n2. **Library Usage**: Always prefer shared libraries over app-specific implementations for common functionality.## 6. Individual App Architecture\n\n**Important**: Each app in &#96;apps/&#96; may follow different internal architectures and frameworks. While the end goal is increased code sharing and consistency, projects are allowed to be different to preserve their unique creative approaches.\n\n### Common Patterns Across Apps\n\n1. **Entry Point**: Most apps use &#96;index.html&#96; as the entry point\n2. **Build Tool**: Vite is the standard build tool across all apps\n3. **Source Structure**: Generally follows &#96;src/&#96; for main code, &#96;css/&#96; for styles, &#96;public/&#96; for assets\n4. **Documentation**: Each app maintains its own documentation in &#96;apps/[app-name]/docs/&#96;\n\n### App-Specific Variations\n\n- **Language**: Some apps use JavaScript, others TypeScript\n- **Framework**: Most use vanilla p5.js, but may incorporate other libraries\n- **Structure**: Internal organization varies based on the app's complexity and purpose\n- **Dependencies**: Each app manages its own specific dependencies\n\n### When Working on Apps\n\n1. **Respect Existing Patterns**: When modifying an app, follow its existing conventions\n2. **App Documentation**: Refer to &#96;apps/[app-name]/docs/&#96; for app-specific guidelines\n3. **Gradual Migration**: If proposing architectural changes, plan gradual migrations rather than major rewrites\n4. **Creative Freedom**: Balance consistency with preserving the creative and experimental nature of each project\n\n## 7. Version Management and Releases\n\n1. **Independent Versioning**: Each app maintains its own version using Nx release configuration\n2. **Conventional Commits**: Use conventional commit format to drive automatic version bumps:\n   - &#96;feat:&#96; for new features (minor version bump)\n   - &#96;fix:&#96; for bug fixes (patch version bump)\n   - &#96;feat!:&#96; or &#96;BREAKING CHANGE:&#96; for breaking changes (major version bump)\n3. **Automatic Changelog**: Each app generates its own &#96;CHANGELOG.md&#96; based on commits\n4. **Release Tags**: Git tags follow the pattern &#96;app-name@version&#96; (e.g., &#96;duo-chrome@1.2.0&#96;)\n5. **Release Commands**:\n   - &#96;nx release --projects=app-name&#96;: Release specific app\n   - &#96;nx release&#96;: Release all apps with changes\n\n## 8. Testing Strategy\n\n### Visual Testing with Playwright\n\n1. **End-to-End Testing**: Use Playwright for testing visual applications and user interactions\n2. **Screenshot Testing**: Capture and compare visual outputs for regression testing\n3. **App-Specific Tests**: Each app can have its own test suite in &#96;tests/&#96; or &#96;e2e/&#96;\n4. **Cross-App Testing**: Shared test utilities in &#96;test/&#96; directory\n\n### Test Commands\n\n- &#96;nx test app-name&#96;: Run tests for specific app\n- &#96;nx run-many --target=test --all&#96;: Run all tests\n- &#96;pnpm test:e2e&#96;: Run end-to-end tests\n- &#96;pnpm test:e2e:ui&#96;: Run tests with Playwright UI\n\n### Creative Testing Considerations\n\n- Test interactive features and user controls\n- Verify save/export functionality works correctly\n- Ensure responsive behavior across different screen sizes\n- Test performance with complex generative algorithms",

{
  "invocationMessage": "Running Get Library Docs",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Ran Get Library Docs ",
  "resultDetails": {
    "input": "{\n  \"context7CompatibleLibraryID\": \"/nrwl/nx\",\n  \"topic\": \"release changelog management monorepo\",\n  \"tokens\": 3000\n}",
    "output": [
      {
        "type": "embed",
        "isText": true,
        "value": "### Changelog Generation with Conventional Commits\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nDemonstrates the generated changelog content when using Conventional Commits. The changelog is automatically populated with features, fixes, and breaking changes based on the commit messages.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n## 1.2.0 (2024-02-09)\n\n### 🚀 Features\n\n- **buttons:** add new background shadow\n\n### ❤️ Thank You\n\n- Juri\n\n## 1.1.0 (2024-02-09)\n\nThis was a version bump only, there were no code changes.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure Nx Release Projects and Versioning\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2025-05-29-mcp-server-with-nx.md\n\nConfigures Nx Release to manage versions for a specific project ('mcp-server') within a monorepo. It sets up manifest roots to update, specifies a pre-version command to run before versioning, and configures project-specific changelogs while disabling workspace-wide changelogs.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"release\": {\n    \"projects\": [\"mcp-server\"],\n    \"version\": {\n      \"manifestRootsToUpdate\": [\n        \"{projectRoot}\",\n        \"{projectRoot}/dist\"\n      ],\n      \"preVersionCommand\": \"npx nx run mcp-server:setup-publish\"\n    },\n    \"changelog\": {\n      \"projectChangelogs\": true,\n      \"workspaceChangelog\": false\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Run Nx Release without Dry Run\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nExecutes the Nx Release command to perform actual versioning, changelog generation, and publishing. This command should be run after configuring any necessary exclusions or settings.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\npnpm nx release --first-release\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure GitHub Release Generation in nx.json\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nThis configuration snippet enables the creation of GitHub releases when running Nx release commands. It requires the &#96;createRelease&#96; property to be set to &#96;github&#96; within the &#96;changelog&#96; configuration. Ensure your repository is pushed to GitHub and changes are present for the release to be created.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    \"release\": {\n        \"projects\": [\"*\", \"!@tuskdesign/demo\"],\n        \"version\": {\n            \"conventionalCommits\": true\n        },\n        \"changelog\": {\n            \"workspaceChangelog\": {\n                \"createRelease\": \"github\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Run Nx Release with Dry Run\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nExecutes the Nx Release command in dry-run mode to simulate versioning, changelog generation, and publishing steps without making actual changes. This is useful for previewing the release process.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\npnpm nx release --dry-run\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Programmatic Nx Release Script in TypeScript\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nThis TypeScript script demonstrates how to use the Nx Release programmatic API to control the versioning, changelog generation, and publishing steps. It utilizes &#96;yargs&#96; for command-line argument parsing, allowing options like &#96;version&#96;, &#96;dryRun&#96;, and &#96;verbose&#96;. The script orchestrates &#96;releaseVersion&#96;, &#96;releaseChangelog&#96;, and &#96;releasePublish&#96; functions.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { releaseChangelog, releasePublish, releaseVersion } from 'nx/release';\nimport * as yargs from 'yargs';\n\n(async () =&gt; {\n  const options = await yargs\n    .version(false) // don't use the default meaning of version in yargs\n    .option('version', {\n      description:\n        'Explicit version specifier to use, if overriding conventional commits',\n      type: 'string',\n    })\n    .option('dryRun', {\n      alias: 'd',\n      description:\n        'Whether or not to perform a dry-run of the release process, defaults to true',\n      type: 'boolean',\n      default: true,\n    })\n    .option('verbose', {\n      description:\n        'Whether or not to enable verbose logging, defaults to false',\n      type: 'boolean',\n      default: false,\n    })\n    .parseAsync();\n\n  const { workspaceVersion, projectsVersionData } = await releaseVersion({\n    specifier: options.version,\n    dryRun: options.dryRun,\n    verbose: options.verbose,\n  });\n\n  await releaseChangelog({\n    versionData: projectsVersionData,\n    version: workspaceVersion,\n    dryRun: options.dryRun,\n    verbose: options.verbose,\n  });\n\n  // The returned number value from releasePublish will be zero if all projects are published successfully, non-zero if not\n  const publishStatus = await releasePublish({\n    dryRun: options.dryRun,\n    verbose: options.verbose,\n  });\n  process.exit(publishStatus);\n})();\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Install JavaScript/TypeScript Versioning Package\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nInstalls the &#96;@nx/js&#96; package at the monorepo root, which is necessary for handling JavaScript/TypeScript package versioning and publishing with Nx Release.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\npnpm add @nx/js -w\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure Independent Releases in nx.json\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/release-projects-independently.md\n\nThis configuration enables independent versioning and publishing for projects in your Nx monorepo. It requires modifying the nx.json file.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"release\": {\n    \"projectsRelationship\": \"independent\"\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Add Nx to Monorepo\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nThis command initializes Nx in an existing monorepo workspace. It might prompt for additional configurations like Project Crystal plugins, which are optional for Nx Release.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\npnpm dlx nx@latest init\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnpx nx@latest init\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Enable Project-Level Changelogs in nx.json\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/release-projects-independently.md\n\nThis configuration enables the generation of individual changelogs for each project when using independent releases. It's an alternative to a single workspace-level CHANGELOG.md file.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"release\": {\n    \"changelog\": {\n      \"projectChangelogs\": true\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Run Nx Release for First Release with Dry Run\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nRuns the Nx Release command with both &#96;--dry-run&#96; and &#96;--first-release&#96; options. This is used when performing the initial release of a repository to handle cases where historical git tag information is unavailable.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\npnpm nx release --dry-run --first-release\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Release Specific Projects using Nx CLI\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/release-projects-independently.md\n\nThis command demonstrates how to use the &#96;--projects&#96; flag with Nx Release to specify a comma-separated list of projects to be versioned and published. It allows releasing only a subset of your monorepo's projects.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnx release --projects=pkg-1,pkg-2\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure Nx Release for Conventional Commits\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nUpdates the 'nx.json' file to enable the Conventional Commits strategy for automated versioning. When enabled, Nx Release determines the next version based on the types of commits (e.g., 'feat', 'fix') in the commit history.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    ...\n    \"release\": {\n        \"projects\": [\"*\", \"!@tuskdesign/demo\"],\n        \"version\": {\n            \"conventionalCommits\": true\n        }\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Nx Release Configuration for Custom Dist Directory Publishing (JSONC)\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/updating-version-references.md\n\nConfiguration within nx.json to set up Nx Release for publishing from a custom distribution directory. It specifies the manifest roots, how to resolve the current version (e.g., from git tags), and importantly, disables the preservation of local dependency protocols to ensure published package.json files are valid. This setup is crucial for managing monorepo package publishing workflows.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsonc\n{\n  \"release\": {\n    \"version\": {\n      \"manifestRootsToUpdate\": [\"dist/packages/{projectName}\"],\n      \"currentVersionResolver\": \"git-tag\",\n      \"preserveLocalDependencyProtocols\": false\n    }\n  },\n  \"targetDefaults\": {\n    \"nx-release-publish\": {\n      \"options\": {\n        \"packageRoot\": \"dist/packages/{projectName}\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Install @monodon/rust Plugin\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/publish-rust-crates.md\n\nInstalls the necessary plugin for Nx Release to manage and release Rust crates within your monorepo. This is a prerequisite for using Nx Release with Rust projects.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnx add @monodon/rust\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Add Nx JavaScript Plugin\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/release-typescript-packages-to-npm.md\n\nInstalls the necessary &#96;@nx/js&#96; package for Nx Release to manage JavaScript packages. Ensure Nx is already installed in your monorepo before running this command.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\nnx add @nx/js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure Nx Release to Exclude Packages\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nModifies the 'nx.json' configuration file to exclude specific packages from the release process. The &#96;release.projects&#96; property accepts an array of glob patterns, allowing for inclusion and exclusion of projects.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n    ...\n    \"release\": {\n        \"projects\": [\"*\", \"!@tuskdesign/demo\"]\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure NPM/Yarn/Bun Workspaces in package.json\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2025-01-28-managing-ts-pkgs-in-monorepos.md\n\nDefines the packages included in the monorepo using glob patterns. This configuration is read by NPM, Yarn, and Bun to manage workspaces.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"name\": \"ts-monorepo-linking\",\n  ...\n  \"workspaces\": [\n    \"apps/*\",\n    \"packages/*\"\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Configure Nx Release for Rust Projects\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/publish-rust-crates.md\n\nConfigures Nx Release to target specific Rust projects for release within your monorepo. This example demonstrates how to release all projects in the 'crates' directory and enables legacy versioning, which is currently required by the @monodon/rust plugin.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"release\": {\n    \"projects\": [\"crates/*\"],\n    \"version\": {\n      \"useLegacyVersioning\": true\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Disable Local CHANGELOG.md File Creation (nx.json)\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/recipes/nx-release/automate-gitlab-releases.md\n\nDisable the generation and management of the local CHANGELOG.md file when using GitLab releases. This configuration ensures that only GitLab releases are used for changelogs.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"release\": {\n    \"changelog\": {\n      \"workspaceChangelog\": {\n        \"file\": false,\n        \"createRelease\": \"gitlab\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Nx Release Workflow with Programmatic API (TypeScript)\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/shared/features/manage-releases.md\n\nThis TypeScript script demonstrates how to use the Nx Release programmatic API to manage a full release cycle. It parses command-line arguments for versioning options, generates version data, creates a changelog, and publishes packages. It relies on 'nx/release' and 'yargs' for functionality and argument parsing.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { releaseChangelog, releasePublish, releaseVersion } from 'nx/release';\nimport * as yargs from 'yargs';\n\n(async () =&gt; {\n  const options = await yargs\n    .version(false) // don't use the default meaning of version in yargs\n    .option('version', {\n      description:\n        'Explicit version specifier to use, if overriding conventional commits',\n      type: 'string',\n    })\n    .option('dryRun', {\n      alias: 'd',\n      description:\n        'Whether or not to perform a dry-run of the release process, defaults to true',\n      type: 'boolean',\n      default: true,\n    })\n    .option('verbose', {\n      description: 'Whether or not to enable verbose logging, defaults to false',\n      type: 'boolean',\n      default: false,\n    })\n    .parseAsync();\n\n  const { workspaceVersion, projectsVersionData } = await releaseVersion({\n    specifier: options.version,\n    dryRun: options.dryRun,\n    verbose: options.verbose,\n  });\n\n  await releaseChangelog({\n    versionData: projectsVersionData,\n    version: workspaceVersion,\n    dryRun: options.dryRun,\n    verbose: options.verbose,\n  });\n\n  // publishResults contains a map of project names and their exit codes\n  const publishResults = await releasePublish({\n    dryRun: options.dryRun,\n    verbose: options.verbose,\n    // You can optionally pass through the version data (e.g. if you are using a custom publish executor that needs to be aware of versions)\n    // It will then be provided to the publish executor options as &#96;nxReleaseVersionData&#96;\n    // This is not required for the default @nx/js publish executor\n    versionData: projectsVersionData,\n  });\n\n  process.exit(\n    Object.values(publishResults).every((result) =&gt; result.code === 0) ? 0 : 1\n  );\n})();\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Commit Changes for Conventional Commits\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-02-09-versioning-and-releasing-packages.md\n\nStages and commits changes to the git repository using a conventional commit message. The format 'feat(scope): description' allows Nx Release to automatically determine the version bump based on the commit type.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;shell\ngit commit -am 'feat(buttons): add new background shadow'\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Nx Dependency Graph with External Nodes\n\nSource: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/docs/blog/2024-08-01-nx-19-5-update.md\n\nIllustrates how Nx recognizes dependencies managed by external package managers like Bun. These are treated as 'externalNodes', meaning Nx will not attempt to build or manage them directly, optimizing the dependency graph for monorepos.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Example showing how Nx might interpret external nodes\n// This is a conceptual representation, actual implementation details may vary.\nconst dependencyGraph = {\n  projects: [\n    // ... other projects\n  ],\n  externalNodes: [\n    // Dependencies managed by Bun, npm, pnpm, yarn\n    { name: 'some-external-package', type: 'npm' },\n    { name: 'another-dep', type: 'bun' }\n  ]\n};\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;"

I need to think through the changelog strategy for a monorepo with independent app releases. Let me analyze the current setup and research best practices. Based on my analysis of your genart monorepo structure and Nx best practices, I can offer you three clear options for changelog management:

## **Option 1: Individual App Changelogs Only (Current Setup)**

**What it is:** Each app maintains its own `CHANGELOG.md`, no monorepo-wide changelog.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Already configured in your Nx setup
- ✅ Perfect independence - each app is self-contained
- ✅ Clean separation for independent deployments
- ✅ Users only see relevant changes for specific apps
- ✅ Minimal maintenance overhead

**Cons:**
- ❌ Shared library changes (@genart/p5-utils, @genart/color-palettes) not tracked
- ❌ Monorepo infrastructure changes (Nx config, tooling, scripts) invisible
- ❌ No central view of what's happening across the monorepo
- ❌ Cross-app improvements or breaking changes hard to communicate

---

## **Option 2: Monorepo-wide Changelog Only**

**What it is:** Single `CHANGELOG.md` at root level tracks all changes across all apps and infrastructure.

**Pros:**
- ✅ Single source of truth for all changes
- ✅ Infrastructure and shared library changes properly tracked
- ✅ Easy to see monorepo evolution over time
- ✅ Cross-app patterns and improvements visible

**Cons:**
- ❌ Can become cluttered with app-specific details
- ❌ Loses independence benefits of apps
- ❌ Harder to filter for specific app changes
- ❌ Goes against Nx's independent release philosophy
- ❌ Potential confusion when apps have different release cycles

---

## **Option 3: Hybrid Approach (Recommended)**

**What it is:** Both individual app changelogs AND a monorepo-wide changelog, each serving different purposes.

**Structure:**
- **App Changelogs** (`CHANGELOG.md`): App-specific features, fixes, UI changes
- **Monorepo Changelog** (root `CHANGELOG.md`): Shared libraries, tooling, infrastructure, cross-app changes

**Pros:**
- ✅ Best of both worlds - independence + visibility
- ✅ Comprehensive tracking of all types of changes
- ✅ Clear separation of concerns
- ✅ Supports Nx's independent release model
- ✅ Shared library updates properly communicated
- ✅ Infrastructure changes documented
- ✅ Flexibility for different audiences (app users vs developers)

**Cons:**
- ❌ More maintenance overhead (but can be automated)
- ❌ Need clear guidelines for what goes where
- ❌ Potential for confusion if boundaries aren't clear

### **Hybrid Implementation Details:**

**Monorepo Changelog would track:**
- Changes to `` (p5-utils, color-palettes, version-display)
- Nx configuration changes
- Build tooling updates (Vite plugin, scripts)
- Cross-app improvements
- Documentation updates
- Testing infrastructure

**App Changelogs would track:**
- New creative features
- App-specific bug fixes
- UI/UX improvements
- App-specific configuration changes
- Performance improvements for that app

---

## **My Recommendation:**

I recommend **Option 3 (Hybrid)** because:
1. Your monorepo has significant shared infrastructure worth tracking
2. Nx naturally supports both `projectChangelogs` and `workspaceChangelog`
3. Your apps are truly independent but share common libraries
4. It matches your intuition: "monorepo-wide changelog would be for nx-level changes, and individual-app changelogs for individual apps"

Which option resonates with you? Once you choose, I'll create a comprehensive plan to update all the documentation, configuration, and instructions to implement it properly.

  "textEditContent": "# Hybrid Changelog Strategy Implementation\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe current monorepo changelog management only supports individual app changelogs, which leaves shared library changes, monorepo infrastructure updates, and cross-app improvements undocumented. We need a comprehensive changelog strategy that maintains app independence while providing visibility into monorepo-wide changes.\n\n## Requirements\n\n### Functional Requirements\n1. **Individual App Changelogs**: Each app maintains its own &#96;CHANGELOG.md&#96; for app-specific changes\n2. **Monorepo Changelog**: Root-level &#96;CHANGELOG.md&#96; for infrastructure and shared library changes\n3. **Clear Boundaries**: Well-defined guidelines for what goes in each changelog type\n4. **Nx Integration**: Leverage Nx's built-in changelog generation capabilities\n5. **Automation**: Minimize manual maintenance through automated changelog generation\n6. **Conventional Commits**: Maintain compatibility with existing conventional commit workflow\n\n### Non-Functional Requirements\n1. **Maintainability**: Clear documentation and guidelines to prevent confusion\n2. **Consistency**: Standardized formatting across all changelogs\n3. **Automation**: Integrate with existing CI/CD and release workflows\n4. **Developer Experience**: Clear instructions for contributors\n\n## Technical Approach\n\n### 1. Nx Configuration Updates\n- Enable both &#96;projectChangelogs&#96; and &#96;workspaceChangelog&#96; in &#96;nx.json&#96;\n- Configure appropriate scoping for monorepo vs app changes\n- Update release configuration to handle hybrid approach\n\n### 2. The plan implements **Option 3: Hybrid Approach** with:

### **Two-Tier Changelog System:**
1. **Monorepo Changelog** (`/CHANGELOG.md`) - For infrastructure, shared libraries, and cross-app changes
2. **Individual App Changelogs** (`apps/{app-name}/CHANGELOG.md`) - For app-specific features and fixes

### **Key Implementation Phases:**

**Phase 1: Configuration and Setup (2-3 hours)**
- Update Nx configuration to enable both changelog types
- Create initial monorepo changelog
- Update core documentation framework

**Phase 2: Guidelines and Processes (3-4 hours)**
- Establish clear change classification system
- Update developer workflows and documentation
- Create decision matrix for changelog routing

**Phase 3: Integration and Testing (2-3 hours)**
- Test hybrid system thoroughly
- Create maintenance documentation
- Validate automation works correctly

### **Clear Scope Definitions:**

**Monorepo Changelog tracks:**
- `` changes (p5-utils, color-palettes, version-display)
- Nx configuration and tooling
- Cross-app improvements
- Documentation and infrastructure

**App Changelogs track:**
- Creative features and algorithms
- App-specific bugs and improvements
- UI/UX changes
- App-specific configuration

### **Risk Mitigation:**
- Clear decision matrix to prevent confusion
- Automated validation tools
- Incremental rollout with testing
- Comprehensive documentation

The plan includes detailed acceptance criteria, timeline estimates (7-10 hours total), and success metrics. It maintains backward compatibility while providing the comprehensive changelog coverage your monorepo needs.

The conversion will follow these steps for each application:\\n\\n1. **Import p5 from p5js-wrapper**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   // For single sketch pattern\\n   import { p5 } from 'p5js-wrapper';\\n   // OR for multi-sketch pattern if needed\\n   import { createSketch } from 'p5js-wrapper';\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n2. **Wrap sketch code in a closure function**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   // From:\\n   function setup() {\\n     createCanvas(800, 600);\\n   }\\n   \\n   // To:\\n   const sketch = (p) =&gt; {\\n     p.setup = function() {\\n       p.createCanvas(800, 600);\\n     }\\n   };\\n   \\n   new p5(sketch);\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n3. **Prefix ALL p5.js functions, variables, and properties with 'p.'**:\\n   - Convert &#96;createCanvas()&#96; to &#96;p.createCanvas()&#96;\\n   - Convert &#96;mouseX&#96; to &#96;p.mouseX&#96;\\n   - Convert &#96;random()&#96; to &#96;p.random()&#96;\\n   - Convert &#96;color()&#96; to &#96;p.color()&#96;\\n   - etc.\\n\\n4. **Convert lifecycle functions to properties of the p5 instance**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   // From:\\n   function setup() { /* ... */ }\\n   function draw() { /* ... */ }\\n   function mousePressed() { /* ... */ }\\n   \\n   // To:\\n   p.setup = function() { /* ... */ }\\n   p.draw = function() { /* ... */ }\\n   p.mousePressed = function() { /* ... */ }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Ensure proper variable scoping**:\\n   - Instance-specific variables should be declared inside the closure\\n   - Truly global variables (shared across instances) should be outside\\n\\n6. **Use dragline as a reference implementation** since it already uses instance mode.\\n\\nFor each app, follow these specific implementation steps:\\n\\na. **duo-chrome**:\\n   - Examine the test directory structure in the PolychromeText app\\n   - Document the configuration patterns and test organization\\n   - Identify reusable components and utilities\\n   - Note how canvas rendering and p5.js-specific elements are tested\\n\\n2. **Install Playwright dependencies**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Install Playwright at the monorepo root level\\n   cd /path/to/monorepo\\n   npm install --save-dev @playwright/test\\n   npx playwright install --with-deps\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n3. **Create shared Playwright configuration**:\\n   - Create a base &#96;playwright.config.ts&#96; file at the monorepo root:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // playwright.config.ts\\n   import { PlaywrightTestConfig } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   const baseConfig: PlaywrightTestConfig = {\\n     testDir: './tests',\\n     timeout: 30000,\\n     forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,\\n     retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,\\n     workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined,\\n     reporter: 'html',\\n     use: {\\n       baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',\\n       trace: 'on-first-retry',\\n       screenshot: 'only-on-failure',\\n     },\\n     projects: [\\n       {\\n         name: 'chromium',\\n         use: { browserName: 'chromium' },\\n       },\\n     ],\\n   };\\n\\n   export default baseConfig;\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n4. **Set up test directory structure**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Create test directories\\n   mkdir -p tests/e2e\\n   mkdir -p tests/utils\\n   mkdir -p tests/fixtures\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Create reusable test utilities**:\\n   - Canvas rendering verification:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/canvas-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function verifyCanvasExists(page: Page): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     await expect(canvas).toBeVisible();\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function verifyCanvasNotEmpty(page: Page): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     // Get canvas and check pixel data\\n     const nonEmptyCanvas = await page.evaluate(() =&gt; {\\n       const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas');\\n       if (!canvas) return false;\\n       \\n       const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');\\n       const data = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height).data;\\n       \\n       // Check if all pixels are transparent/empty\\n       for (let i = 3; i &lt; data.length; i += 4) {\\n         if (data[i] !== 0) return true;\\n       }\\n       return false;\\n     });\\n     \\n     expect(nonEmptyCanvas).toBeTruthy();\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Keyboard interaction helpers:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/keyboard-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function pressKeyAndWait(page: Page, key: string, waitTime = 100): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     await page.keyboard.press(key);\\n     await page.waitForTimeout(waitTime);\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function typeTextAndWait(page: Page, text: string, waitTime = 100): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     await page.keyboard.type(text);\\n     await page.waitForTimeout(waitTime);\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Mouse interaction helpers:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/mouse-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function clickCanvasAt(page: Page, x: number, y: number): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const box = await canvas.boundingBox();\\n     \\n     if (!box) throw new Error('Canvas not found');\\n     \\n     await page.mouse.click(box.x + x, box.y + y);\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function dragOnCanvas(page: Page, startX: number, startY: number, endX: number, endY: number): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const box = await canvas.boundingBox();\\n     \\n     if (!box) throw new Error('Canvas not found');\\n     \\n     await page.mouse.move(box.x + startX, box.y + startY);\\n     await page.mouse.down();\\n     await page.mouse.move(box.x + endX, box.y + endY);\\n     await page.mouse.up();\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Screenshot comparison utilities:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/screenshot-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import path from 'path';\\n\\n   export async function compareScreenshot(page: Page, screenshotName: string, threshold = 0.2): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const screenshotPath = path.join('tests', 'screenshots', 'reference', &#96;${screenshotName}.png&#96;);\\n     \\n     await expect(page.locator('canvas')).toHaveScreenshot(screenshotName + '.png', {\\n       maxDiffPixelRatio: threshold,\\n     });\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function captureCanvasScreenshot(page: Page, screenshotName: string): Promise&lt;string&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const screenshotPath = path.join('tests', 'screenshots', 'actual', &#96;${screenshotName}.png&#96;);\\n     \\n     await canvas.screenshot({ path: screenshotPath });\\n     return screenshotPath;\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n6. **Document the testing approach**:\\n   - Create a comprehensive testing guide at &#96;docs/testing/playwright-guide.md&#96;:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Playwright Testing Guide for p5.js Apps\\n\\n   This guide explains how to write and run Playwright tests for p5.js applications in the monorepo.\\n\\n   ## Getting Started\\n\\n   ### Running Tests\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Run all tests\\n   nx run-many --target=e2e --all\\n   \\n   # Run tests for a specific app\\n   nx run those-shape-things:e2e\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   ## Test Structure\\n   \\n   Tests are organized as follows:\\n   - &#96;tests/e2e/&#96;: End-to-end tests for applications\\n   - &#96;tests/utils/&#96;: Shared test utilities\\n   - &#96;tests/fixtures/&#96;: Test data and fixtures\\n\\n   ## Writing Tests for p5.js Apps\\n\\n   ### Canvas Testing\\n   \\n   Canvas elements require special handling. Use the provided utilities:\\n\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import { verifyCanvasExists, verifyCanvasNotEmpty } from 'module',\\n     plugins: ['jsx', 'typescript']\\n   });\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   \\n   - Parse JavaScript code into an AST\\n   - Traverse the AST to identify:\\n     - Global p5.js function calls (e.g., &#96;rect()&#96;, &#96;ellipse()&#96;)\\n     - Property accesses (e.g., &#96;width&#96;, &#96;height&#96;)\\n     - Constants (e.g., &#96;CENTER&#96;, &#96;PI&#96;)\\n     - Lifecycle function declarations\\n     - Import statements\\n\\n4. **Transformation Logic**:\\n   - Add &#96;p.&#96; prefix to all p5.js functions, properties, and constants\\n   - Convert lifecycle functions to instance mode format:\\n     &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n     // From:\\n     function setup() {\\n       createCanvas(400, 400);\\n     }\\n     \\n     // To:\\n     p.setup = function() {\\n       p.createCanvas(400, 400);\\n     };\\n     &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Wrap the entire sketch in an instance mode closure:\\n     &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n     new p5(function(p) {\\n       // Converted sketch code here\\n     });\\n     &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Update import statements to use p5js-wrapper:\\n     &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n     // From:\\n     import p5 from 'p5';\\n     \\n     // To:\\n     import { p5 } from 'p5js-wrapper';\\n     &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Edge Case Handling**:\\n   - Preserve non-p5 code unchanged\\n   - Handle nested function calls correctly\\n   - Maintain - Implement a dry-run mode that shows changes without applying them\\n   - Create automatic backups of original files\\n   - Add syntax validation to ensure output code is valid JavaScript\\n   - .version('1.0.0')\\n     .description('Convert p5.js code from global mode to instance mode')\\n     .option('-i, --input &lt;file&gt;', 'Input file path')\\n     .option('-o, --output &lt;file&gt;', \"details\": \"This task involves implementing an automated version management system for all applications in the monorepo:\\n\\n1. **Version Management Strategy**:\\n   - Implement semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) across all apps\\n   - Update only apps that have actual changes (not all apps every time)\\n   - Use standard npm versioning commands (&#96;npm version patch|minor|major&#96;)\\n   - Define policies for when to increment each version component\\n\\n2. **Nx Integration for Change Detection**:\\n   - Leverage Nx's affected detection to identify which apps have changes\\n   - Use &#96;nx affected:apps&#96; to determine which apps need version bumps\\n   - Create a simple script that:\\n     - Detects affected apps using Nx commands\\n     - Runs appropriate npm version commands in each affected app directory\\n     - Commits version changes\\n   \\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   // Example implementation in version-update.js\\n   const { execSync } = require('child_process');\\n   \\n   function updateVersions(versionBump = 'patch') {\\n     // Get affected apps using Nx\\n     const affectedOutput = execSync('npx nx affected:apps').toString();\\n     const affectedApps = affectedOutput.trim().split('\\\\n');\\n     \\n     if (affectedApps.length === 0 || (affectedApps.length === 1 &amp;&amp; !affectedApps[0])) {\\n       console.log('No affected apps detected. Skipping version updates.');\\n       return;\\n     }\\n     \\n     console.log(&#96;Updating versions for affected apps: ${affectedApps.join(', ')}&#96;);\\n     \\n     // Update version for each affected app\\n     affectedApps.forEach(appName =&gt; {\\n       const appPath = &#96;apps/${appName}&#96;;\\n       console.log(&#96;Updating ${appName} with npm version ${versionBump}&#96;);\\n       try {\\n         execSync(&#96;cd ${appPath} &amp;&amp; npm version ${versionBump} --no-git-tag-version&#96;);\\n       } catch (error) {\\n         console.error(&#96;Error updating version for ${appName}:&#96;, error.message);\\n       }\\n     });\\n     \\n     // Optionally commit changes\\n     console.log('Version updates complete. Remember to commit the changes.');\\n   }\\n   \\n   // Parse command line arguments\\n   const args = process.argv.slice(2);\\n   const versionBump = args[0] || 'patch';\\n   updateVersions(versionBump);\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n3. **Integration with Build/Release Process**:\\n   - \"status\": \"pending\",\n        \"priority\": \"medium\",\n        \"dependencies\": [\n          \"30\"\n        ],\n        \"details\": \"This task involves conducting a comprehensive audit of package.json files in the monorepo:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   const fs = require('fs');\\n   const path = require('path');\\n   const glob = require('glob');\\n   \\n   // Read workspace root package.json\\n   const rootPkg = require('./package.json');\\n   const rootDeps = {...rootPkg.dependencies, ...rootPkg.devDependencies};\\n   \\n   // Find all app package.json files\\n   const appPackageJsons = glob.sync('./apps/*/package.json');\\n   \\n   const analysis = {\\n     duplicates: [],\\n     versionMismatches: [],\\n     appSpecific: {},\\n     unused: []\\n   };\\n   \\n   appPackageJsons.forEach(pkgPath =&gt; {\\n     const appName = path.dirname(pkgPath).split('/').pop();\\n     const appPkg = require(pkgPath);\\n     const appDeps = {...appPkg.dependencies, ...appPkg.devDependencies};\\n     \\n     analysis.appSpecific[appName] = [];\\n     \\n     // Check for duplicates and mismatches\\n     Object.entries(appDeps).forEach(([dep, version]) =&gt; {\\n       if (rootDeps[dep]) {\\n         analysis.duplicates.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         \\n         if (version !== rootDeps[dep]) {\\n           analysis.versionMismatches.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         }\\n       } else {\\n         analysis.appSpecific[appName].push({dep, version});\\n       }\\n     });\\n   });\\n   \\n   // Output analysis results\\n   console.log(JSON.stringify(analysis, null, 2));\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n2. **Dependency Categorization**:\\n   - Identify build tools that should be managed at workspace level only:\\n     - Vite, ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, Nx, Jest, Playwright, etc.\\n   - Identify runtime dependencies that should be shared:\\n     - React, p5.js, common UI libraries, utility libraries\\n   - Identify app-specific dependencies that should remain local:\\n     - Specialized libraries used by only one app\\n     - App-specific plugins or extensions\\n\\n3. **Dependency Cleanup**:\\n   - Move all build tools to workspace root package.json:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Example: moving ESLint from app to root\\n   npm uninstall eslint --workspace=app-name\\n   npm install eslint --save-dev\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Standardize versions for shared dependencies:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Update all apps to use the same version as root\\n   npm install react@workspace-version --workspace=app-name\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Remove unused dependencies identified during analysis\\n   - Keep truly app-specific dependencies in their respective package.json files\\n\\n4. **Documentation Update**:\\n   - Create a dependency management strategy document in docs/architecture/:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Dependency Management Strategy\\n   \\n   ## Workspace-level Dependencies\\n   - **Build Tools**: All build tools (Vite, ESLint, TypeScript, etc.) are managed at the workspace level\\n   - **Shared Runtime Dependencies**: Common libraries used across multiple apps\\n   \\n   ## App-level Dependencies\\n   - Only dependencies that are truly specific to a single app\\n   - Must not duplicate workspace dependencies\\n   \\n   ## Adding New Dependencies\\n   1. Determine if the dependency will be used by multiple apps\\n      - If yes: Add to workspace root\\n      - If no: Add to specific app\\n   \\n   ## Version Management\\n   - All shared dependencies must use the same version across the workspace\\n   - Version upgrades should be coordinated across all affected packages\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   \\n   - Update adding-projects.md with clear guidelines:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   ## Dependency Management\\n   \\n   When adding dependencies to your project:\\n   \\n   1. #!/usr/bin/env node
/*
  Simple workspace changelog aggregator for Nx independent-project workspaces.
  - Scans apps/*/CHANGELOG.md
  - Collects entries that look like infra/shared changes (keywords)
  - Emits a merged changelog section to stdout or writes to /CHANGELOG.md when --apply is set

  Usage:
    node scripts/generate-workspace-changelog.js [--apply] [--out ./CHANGELOG.md]

*/
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const ROOT = process.cwd();
const APPS_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'apps');
const OUT_FILE = process.argv.includes('--out') ? process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--out')+1] : path.join(ROOT, 'CHANGELOG.md');
const APPLY = process.argv.includes('--apply');

const KEYWORDS = [
  'nx.json', 'nx', 'monorepo', 'workspace', 'libs/', 'lib/', 'docs/', 'build', 'ci', 'chore(release)', 'version', 'release', 'deploy'
];

function containsKeyword(line) {
  const l = line.toLowerCase();
  return KEYWORDS.some(k => l.includes(k));
}

async function collectFromChangelog(filePath) {
  try {
    const txt = await fs.promises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8');
    const lines = txt.split(/\r?\n/);

    // find Unreleased section first
    const entries = [];
    let inUnreleased = false;
    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
      const line = lines[i];
      if (/^##\s+\[?Unreleased\]?/i.test(line)) {
        inUnreleased = true;
        continue;
      }
      if (inUnreleased) {
        if (/^##\s+\[?\d+/.test(line)) break; // next version
        if (/^\s*-\s+/.test(line) || /^\s*\*/.test(line)) {
          if (containsKeyword(line)) entries.push(line.trim());
        }
      }
    }

    // fallback: scan recent releases for infra keywords
    if (entries.length === 0) {
      let capturing = false;
      for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
        const line = lines[i];
        if (/^##\s+\[?\d+/.test(line)) {
          capturing = true; // after first version heading
          continue;
        }
        if (capturing && (/^\s*-\s+/.test(line) || /^\s*\*/.test(line))) {
          if (containsKeyword(line)) entries.push(line.trim());
        }
        if (entries.length >= 20) break;
      }
    }

    return entries;
  } catch (e) {
    return [];
  }
}

async function main() {
  const apps = await fs.promises.readdir(APPS_DIR, { withFileTypes: true });
  const collected = {};

  for (const d of apps) {
    if (!d.isDirectory()) continue;
    const changelogPath = path.join(APPS_DIR, d.name, 'CHANGELOG.md');
    if (fs.existsSync(changelogPath)) {
      const entries = await collectFromChangelog(changelogPath);
      if (entries.length) collected[d.name] = entries;
    }
  }

  // Build workspace changelog content
  const header = `# Monorepo Changelog\n\nThis changelog aggregates infrastructure and shared-library changes across the workspace.\n\n## Unreleased\n\n`;

  const infraHeader = '### Infrastructure & Shared Libraries\n\n';
  let body = header + infraHeader;
  let any = false;
  for (const [app, entries] of Object.entries(collected)) {
    const filtered = entries.filter(Boolean);
    if (filtered.length) {
      any = true;
      body += `- From **${app}**:\n`;
      for (const e of filtered) {
        // normalize leading '- '
        const normalized = e.replace(/^[-*]\s+/, '');
        body += `  - ${normalized}\n`;
      }
      body += '\n';
    }
  }

  if (!any) {
    body += '- No infra/shared-library entries detected in app changelogs.\n\n';
  }

  body += '\n## Notes\n\n- This file is generated by `scripts/generate-workspace-changelog.js`.\n- The generator looks for keywords in app changelogs and aggregates likely workspace-scoped changes.\n';

  if (APPLY) {
    // If file exists, merge Unreleased section
    let existing = '';
    if (fs.existsSync(OUT_FILE)) existing = await fs.promises.readFile(OUT_FILE, 'utf8');
    // naive replace or prepend: if file contains '## Unreleased' replace that block, else prepend
    let out = '';
    if (/##\s+Unreleased/i.test(existing)) {
      out = existing.replace(/##\s+Unreleased[\s\S]*?(?=^##\s+|$)/im, '## Unreleased\n\n' + infraHeader + '\n');
      // if replacement didn't inject content, just prepend
      if (out === existing) out = body + '\n' + existing;
    } else {
      out = body + '\n' + existing;
    }
    await fs.promises.writeFile(OUT_FILE, out, 'utf8');
    console.log(`Wrote workspace changelog to ${OUT_FILE}`);
  } else {
    console.log(body);
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e);
  process.exit(1);
});

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Simple workspace changelog aggregator for Nx independent-project workspaces.
// Scans apps/*/CHANGELOG.md and collects likely infra/shared changes.
// Usage: node scripts/generate-workspace-changelog.js [--apply] [--out ./CHANGELOG.md]
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const ROOT = process.cwd();
const APPS_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'apps');
const OUT_FILE = process.argv.includes('--out') ? process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--out')+1] : path.join(ROOT, 'CHANGELOG.md');
const APPLY = process.argv.includes('--apply');

const KEYWORDS = [
  'nx.json', 'nx', 'monorepo', 'workspace', 'libs/', 'lib/', 'docs/', 'build', 'ci', 'chore(release)', 'version', 'release', 'deploy'
];

function containsKeyword(line) {
  const l = line.toLowerCase();
  return KEYWORDS.some(k => l.includes(k));
}

async function collectFromChangelog(filePath) {
  try {
    const txt = await fs.promises.readFile(filePath, 'utf8');
    const lines = txt.split(/\r?\n/);

    // find Unreleased section first
    const entries = [];
    let inUnreleased = false;
    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
      const line = lines[i];
      if (/^##\s+\[?Unreleased\]?/i.test(line)) {
        inUnreleased = true;
        continue;
      }
      if (inUnreleased) {
        if (/^##\s+\[?\d+/.test(line)) break; // next version
        if (/^\s*-\s+/.test(line) || /^\s*\*/.test(line)) {
          if (containsKeyword(line)) entries.push(line.trim());
        }
      }
    }

    // fallback: scan recent releases for infra keywords
    if (entries.length === 0) {
      let capturing = false;
      for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
        const line = lines[i];
        if (/^##\s+\[?\d+/.test(line)) {
          capturing = true; // after first version heading
          continue;
        }
        if (capturing && (/^\s*-\s+/.test(line) || /^\s*\*/.test(line))) {
          if (containsKeyword(line)) entries.push(line.trim());
        }
        if (entries.length >= 20) break;
      }
    }

    return entries;
  } catch (e) {
    return [];
  }
}

async function main() {
  const apps = await fs.promises.readdir(APPS_DIR, { withFileTypes: true });
  const collected = {};

  for (const d of apps) {
    if (!d.isDirectory()) continue;
    const changelogPath = path.join(APPS_DIR, d.name, 'CHANGELOG.md');
    if (fs.existsSync(changelogPath)) {
      const entries = await collectFromChangelog(changelogPath);
      if (entries.length) collected[d.name] = entries;
    }
  }

  // Build workspace changelog content
  const header = `# Monorepo Changelog\n\nThis changelog aggregates infrastructure and shared-library changes across the workspace.\n\n## Unreleased\n\n`;

  const infraHeader = '### Infrastructure & Shared Libraries\n\n';
  let body = header + infraHeader;
  let any = false;
  for (const [app, entries] of Object.entries(collected)) {
    const filtered = entries.filter(Boolean);
    if (filtered.length) {
      any = true;
      body += `- From **${app}**:\n`;
      for (const e of filtered) {
        // normalize leading '- '
        const normalized = e.replace(/^[-*]\s+/, '');
        body += `  - ${normalized}\n`;
      }
      body += '\n';
    }
  }

  if (!any) {
    body += '- No infra/shared-library entries detected in app changelogs.\n\n';
  }

  body += '\n## Notes\n\n- This file is generated by `scripts/generate-workspace-changelog.js`.\n- The generator looks for keywords in app changelogs and aggregates likely workspace-scoped changes.\n';

  if (APPLY) {
    // If file exists, merge Unreleased section
    let existing = '';
    if (fs.existsSync(OUT_FILE)) existing = await fs.promises.readFile(OUT_FILE, 'utf8');
    // naive replace or prepend: if file contains '## Unreleased' replace that block, else prepend
    let out = '';
    if (/##\s+Unreleased/i.test(existing)) {
      out = existing.replace(/##\s+Unreleased[\s\S]*?(?=^##\s+|$)/im, '## Unreleased\n\n' + infraHeader + '\n');
      // if replacement didn't inject content, just prepend
      if (out === existing) out = body + '\n' + existing;
    } else {
      out = body + '\n' + existing;
    }
    await fs.promises.writeFile(OUT_FILE, out, 'utf8');
    console.log(`Wrote workspace changelog to ${OUT_FILE}`);
  } else {
    console.log(body);
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e);
  process.exit(1);
});

```

Modify the &#96;KEYWORDS&#96; array in &#96;scripts/generate-workspace-changelog.js&#96;\n2. Test with existing changelogs to verify effectiveness\n3. Update this documentation\n4. Commit with scope &#96;feat(monorepo): update changelog classification keywords&#96;\n\n### Regular Review\n- Monthly: Review misclassified entries and update guidelines\n- Quarterly: Evaluate keyword effectiveness and suggest improvements\n- Release cycles: Validate that hybrid approach serves release documentation needs\n\n## Integration with Release Process\n\n### Automated Workflow\n1. Developers create commits following classification guidelines\n2. App-specific changes go to app changelogs via Nx release process\n3. Infrastructure changes are detected and aggregated via the workspace changelog script\n4. ```markdown
# Changelog Management

## Hybrid Changelog System

The GenArt monorepo uses a **hybrid changelog approach** with both workspace-level and app-specific changelogs:

- **Monorepo Changelog** (`/CHANGELOG.md`): Infrastructure, shared libraries, and cross-app changes
- **App Changelogs** (`apps/[app-name]/CHANGELOG.md`): App-specific features, fixes, and improvements

### Automated Classification
Changes are automatically routed based on keywords in commit messages. See [`docs/changelog-classification-system.md`](../docs/changelog-classification-system.md) for detailed classification rules.

### Quick Reference: Where Does My Change Go?

| Change Type | Changelog Location | Keywords/Indicators |
|-------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Shared library changes | Monorepo | `libs/`, `lib/` |
| Nx configuration | Monorepo | `nx.json`, `nx`, `workspace` |
| Build/deployment | Monorepo | `build`, `ci`, `deploy`, `release` |
| Documentation | Monorepo | `docs/` (root-level docs) |
| App features | App-specific | App name in scope, no infrastructure keywords |
| App UI/UX | App-specific | App-specific improvements |
| App dependencies | App-specific | `apps/[app]/package.json` changes |

## Automation Rules

**Before any git commit**, ask: "Should I create a changelog entry for these changes?"

For significant non-commit changes, ask: "These changes seem substantial enough to warrant a changelog entry. Create one?"

**Include in changelog:**
- API endpoint changes
- Frontend features or UI changes  
- User-facing bug fixes
- Documentation that affects end users
- Breaking changes or security fixes
- Infrastructure improvements (monorepo changelog)
- Shared library additions/changes (monorepo changelog)

**Exclude from changelog:**
- Internal refactoring, tests, build changes (unless they affect user experience)
- LLM instruction updates
- Code comments or internal docs

## Semantic Versioning

- **MAJOR**: Breaking changes, API incompatibilities
- **MINOR**: New features, backwards-compatible additions  
- **PATCH**: Bug fixes, backwards-compatible changes

Default to PATCH increment on commits with changelog entries. Ask user to confirm MINOR/MAJOR bumps.

## Format

### Monorepo Changelog Format

```markdown
# Monorepo Changelog

This changelog aggregates infrastructure and shared-library changes across the workspace.

## Unreleased

### Infrastructure & Shared Libraries

- **monorepo:** add hybrid changelog generation system
- **libs/p5-utils:** add new canvas utility functions
- **build:** update Vite configuration for all apps

## Notes

- This file is generated by `scripts/generate-workspace-changelog.js`.
- The generator looks for keywords in app changelogs and aggregates likely workspace-scoped changes.
```

### App Changelog Format

Use keepachangelog.com format in `apps/[app-name]/CHANGELOG.md`:

```markdown
# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- New features

### Changed  
- Modified functionality

### Fixed
- Bug fixes

### Security
- Security improvements

## [1.0.0] - 2024-01-01
### Added
- Initial release
```
```

```markdown
## Workflow Integration

### Automated Changelog Generation

1. **App Changelogs**: Generated automatically by Nx release process
2. **Monorepo Changelog**: Generated by workspace aggregator script

```bash
# Generate workspace changelog (dry-run)
pnpm gen:changelog

# Apply workspace changelog updates  
pnpm gen:changelog:apply
```

### Manual Changelog Updates

For edge cases or when automated classification needs override:

1. **App Changelogs**: Edit `apps/[app-name]/CHANGELOG.md` directly
2. **Monorepo Changelog**: Edit `/CHANGELOG.md` directly or update and re-run aggregator

### Release Process Integration

1. Developers create commits following classification guidelines
2. Nx release process generates app-specific changelogs
3. Workspace aggregator script collects infrastructure changes
4. Both changelog types are updated during release

## Entry Guidelines

Write clear, user-focused entries:
- "Board archiving functionality with restore option"
- "New GET /api/boards/:id/archive endpoint"  
- "Fixed card drag-and-drop position errors"
- "Updated shared color palette utilities"
- "Improved Nx workspace configuration"

Avoid vague entries like "Updated some stuff" or "Fixed bugs".

## Classification Examples

### Monorepo Changelog Commits
```bash
feat(libs/p5-utils): add pressure-sensitive drawing utilities
fix(nx): resolve workspace release configuration  
chore(build): update Vite config for all apps
docs(monorepo): improve development workflow guide
```

### App Changelog Commits  
```bash
feat(duo-chrome): add color inversion feature
fix(dragline): resolve mouse tracking accuracy
perf(computational-collage): optimize image processing  
docs(crude-collage): update user interaction guide
```

For detailed classification rules, see [`docs/changelog-classification-system.md`](../docs/changelog-classification-system.md).
```

</tool-use>

    \"title\": \"Audit and Optimize Package Dependencies Across Workspace\",\n        \"description\": \"Review all app package.json files against workspace root package.json to identify and resolve duplications, version mismatches, and optimize dependency management across the monorepo.\",\n        \"status\": \"pending\",\n        \"priority\": \"medium\",\n        \"dependencies\": [\n          \"30\"\n        ],\n        \"details\": \"This task involves conducting a comprehensive audit of dependencies across the monorepo to establish a clean separation between workspace-level and app-specific dependencies:\\n\\n1. **Dependency Analysis**:\\n   - Create a script to analyze all package.json files in the monorepo:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   const fs = require('fs');\\n   const path = require('path');\\n   const glob = require('glob');\\n   \\n   // Read workspace root package.json\\n   const rootPkg = require('./package.json');\\n   const rootDeps = {...rootPkg.dependencies, ...rootPkg.devDependencies};\\n   \\n   // Find all app package.json files\\n   const appPackageJsons = glob.sync('./apps/*/package.json');\\n   \\n   const analysis = {\\n     duplicates: [],\\n     versionMismatches: [],\\n     appSpecific: {},\\n     unused: []\\n   };\\n   \\n   appPackageJsons.forEach(pkgPath =&gt; {\\n     const appName = path.dirname(pkgPath).split('/').pop();\\n     const appPkg = require(pkgPath);\\n     const appDeps = {...appPkg.dependencies, ...appPkg.devDependencies};\\n     \\n     analysis.appSpecific[appName] = [];\\n     \\n     // Check for duplicates and mismatches\\n     Object.entries(appDeps).forEach(([dep, version]) =&gt; {\\n       if (rootDeps[dep]) {\\n         analysis.duplicates.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         \\n         if (version !== rootDeps[dep]) {\\n           analysis.versionMismatches.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         }\\n       } else {\\n         analysis.appSpecific[appName].push({dep, version});\\n       }\\n     });\\n   });\\n   \\n   // Output analysis results\\n   console.log(JSON.stringify(analysis, null, 2));\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n2. **Dependency Categorization**:\\n   - Identify build tools that should be managed at workspace level only:\\n     - Vite, ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, Nx, Jest, Playwright, etc.\\n   - Identify runtime dependencies that should be shared:\\n     - React, p5.js, common UI libraries, utility libraries\\n   - Identify app-specific dependencies that should remain local:\\n     - Specialized libraries used by only one app\\n     - App-specific plugins or extensions\\n\\n3. **Dependency Cleanup**:\\n   - Move all build tools to workspace root package.json:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Example: moving ESLint from app to root\\n   npm uninstall eslint --workspace=app-name\\n   npm install eslint --save-dev\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Standardize versions for shared dependencies:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Update all apps to use the same version as root\\n   npm install react@workspace-version --workspace=app-name\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Remove unused dependencies identified during analysis\\n   - Keep truly app-specific dependencies in their respective package.json files\\n\\n4. **Documentation Update**:\\n   - Create a dependency management strategy document in docs/architecture/:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Dependency Management Strategy\\n   \\n   ## Workspace-level Dependencies\\n   - **Build Tools**: All build tools (Vite, ESLint, TypeScript, etc.) are managed at the workspace level\\n   - **Shared Runtime Dependencies**: Common libraries used across multiple apps\\n   \\n   ## App-level Dependencies\\n   - Only dependencies that are truly specific to a single app\\n   - Must not duplicate workspace dependencies\\n   \\n   ## Adding New Dependencies\\n   1. Determine if the dependency will be used by multiple apps\\n      - If yes: Add to workspace root\\n      - If no: Add to specific app\\n   \\n   ## Version Management\\n   - All shared dependencies must use the same version across the workspace\\n   - Version upgrades should be coordinated across all affected packages\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   \\n   - Update adding-projects.md with clear guidelines:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   ## Dependency Management\\n   \\n   When adding dependencies to your project:\\n   \\n   1. Check if the dependency already exists in the workspace root\\n      - If yes: Do not add it to your app's package.json\\n   \\n   2. For build tools (Vite, ESLint, etc.):\\n      - These should only be added to workspace root\\n      - Configure as needed in your app\\n   \\n   3. For app-specific dependencies:\\n      - Add only to your app's package.json\\n      - Document why this dependency is needed\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Testing and Verification**:\\n   - Run builds for all apps to ensure they still function correctly\\n   - Verify that dependency hoisting works as expected\\n   - Check for any resolution warnings or errors\",\n        \"testStrategy\": \"1. **Dependency Analysis Verification**:\\n   - Run the analysis script and verify it correctly identifies:\\n     - All duplicated dependencies between apps and workspace root\\n     - All version mismatches between apps and workspace root\\n     - App-specific dependencies that should remain local\\n     - Potentially unused dependencies\\n   - Cross-check results with manual inspection of package.json files\\n\\n2. **Build Tool Migration Testing**:\\n   - After moving build tools to workspace root:\\n     - Run &#96;npm run build&#96; &#96;.github/changelog-management.md&#96;.\n3.  **Determine Changelog Type:** Classify changes using the hybrid changelog system:\n    - **Monorepo Changelog** (&#96;/CHANGELOG.md&#96;): standardize version display across apps&#96; |\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n",
  "textEditContent": "### **Mandatory Git Commit Workflow**\n\nWhen you are asked to create a commit, you **MUST** follow these steps in order:\n\n1.  **Analyze Changes:** Run &#96;git status&#96; and &#96;git diff --staged&#96; to understand the modifications.\n2.  **Evaluate for Changelog:** Review the changes against the criteria in &#96;.github/changelog-management.md&#96;.\n3.  **Determine Changelog Type:** Classify changes using the hybrid changelog system:\n    - **Monorepo Changelog** (&#96;/CHANGELOG.md&#96;): Infrastructure, shared libraries, Nx config, build tools, cross-app changes\n    - **App Changelog** (&#96;apps/[app]/CHANGELOG.md&#96;): App-specific features, fixes, UI changes\n4.  **Ask About Changelog:** If the changes meet the criteria (e.g., new features, UI changes, bug fixes), you **MUST** ask the user: \"Should I create a changelog entry for these changes?\" You may also provide advice on whether an entry seems warranted and which changelog it should go to.\n5.  **Create Changelog (if approved):** If the user agrees, update the appropriate changelog(s) according to the hybrid system.\n6.  **Propose Commit Message:** After handling the changelog, draft a commit message that follows the Conventional Commits specification with proper scope for changelog routing.\n7.  **Commit Changes:** After the user approves the message, stage any modified changelog files and run &#96;git commit&#96;.\n\n### See &#96;./changelog-management.md&#96; for detailed instructions on pre-commit changelog rules.\n\n### Commit Message Guidelines for Hybrid Changelogs\n\nFollow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification with these scope patterns for proper changelog routing:\n\n#### **Monorepo Changelog Routing**\nUse these scopes and keywords to route changes to the workspace changelog:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Infrastructure and build changes\nfeat(monorepo): implement hybrid changelog generation system\nfix(nx): resolve workspace release configuration conflicts\nchore(build): update Vite configuration for all apps\ndocs(workspace): update development workflow guidelines\n\n# Shared library changes  \nfeat(libs/p5-utils): add pressure-sensitive drawing utilities\nfix(libs/color-palettes): resolve RISO color mapping issue\nperf(libs/version-display): optimize component rendering\n\n# Cross-app improvements\nfeat(workspace): add automated screenshot generation\nfix(monorepo): resolve inter-app dependency issues\nchore(release): update version bump automation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### **App Changelog Routing**\nUse app names in scope for app-specific changes:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# App-specific features and fixes\nfeat(duo-chrome): add color inversion feature  \nfix(dragline): resolve mouse tracking accuracy issues\nperf(computational-collage): optimize image processing\ndocs(crude-collage): update user interaction guide\n\n# App-specific UI and functionality\nfeat(monochromifier): add save-as-transparent option\nfix(those-shape-things): resolve shape rotation bug\nstyle(duo-chrome): improve responsive layout\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### **Edge Cases and Multi-Area Changes**\nFor changes affecting both shared components and specific apps:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Primary impact determines changelog (shared lib = monorepo)\nfeat(libs/p5-utils): add drawing function, update duo-chrome integration\n\n# Breaking changes affecting multiple apps\nfeat(monorepo)!: update shared color palette API across all apps\n\n# Documentation spanning multiple areas  \ndocs(monorepo): update app integration workflow and examples\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### **Commit Message Best Practices**\n\n1. **Use Descriptive Scopes**: Choose scopes that clearly indicate the area of impact\n2. **Include Keywords**: For monorepo routing, include infrastructure keywords in commit messages\n3. **Be Specific**: Avoid generic scopes like \"misc\" or \"various\"\n4. **Conventional Format**: Always follow &#96;type(scope): description&#96; format\n5. **Breaking Changes**: Use &#96;!&#96; or &#96;BREAKING CHANGE:&#96; footer for major changes\n\n#### **Examples by Change Type**\n\n| Change Type | Scope Pattern | Example |\n|-------------|---------------|---------|\n| New shared library | &#96;libs/[library-name]&#96; | &#96;feat(libs/p5-utils): add canvas export utilities&#96; |\n| Nx configuration | &#96;nx&#96;, &#96;workspace&#96;, &#96;monorepo&#96; | &#96;feat(nx): add workspace changelog support&#96; |\n| Build system | &#96;build&#96;, &#96;ci&#96;, &#96;deploy&#96; | &#96;fix(build): resolve Vite configuration conflicts&#96; |\n| Documentation | &#96;docs(monorepo)&#96; or &#96;docs(app-name)&#96; | &#96;docs(monorepo): update hybrid changelog workflow&#96; |\n| App feature | &#96;app-name&#96; | &#96;feat(duo-chrome): implement layer system&#96; |\n| App bug fix | &#96;app-name&#96; | &#96;fix(crude-collage): resolve canvas resize issues&#96; |\n| Cross-app change | &#96;monorepo&#96;, &#96;workspace&#96; | &#96;feat(monorepo): standardize version display across apps&#96; |",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

libraries&lt;br/&gt;libs/* ?}\n    B --&gt;|Yes| C[📝 Monorepo Changelog]\n    B --&gt;|No| D{Does it affect Nx configuration&lt;br/&gt;nx.json, workspace setup?}\n    D --&gt;|Yes| C\n    D --&gt;|No|
