(features, UI, fixes)? | 📱 **App Changelog** | ⬇️ Next Question |\n| **Does it have cross-app impact** (affects multiple apps)? | 📝 **Monorepo Changelog** | ❓ **Ask for guidance** |\n\n## 🎯 Quick Reference by File Path\n\n### 📝 Monorepo Changelog (&#96;/CHANGELOG.md&#96;)\n- &#96;libs/&#96; - Any shared library changes\n- &#96;nx.json&#96; - Nx workspace configuration\n- &#96;package.json&#96; (root) - Workspace dependencies\n- &#96;docs/&#96; - Workspace-wide documentation\n- &#96;tools/&#96; - Build tools and utilities\n- &#96;scripts/&#96; - Workspace scripts\n- &#96;.github/&#96; - CI/CD, templates, workflows\n\n### 📱 App Changelog (&#96;apps/[app]/CHANGELOG.md&#96;)\n- &#96;apps/[specific-app]/&#96; - App-specific changes\n- App features, UI improvements, bug fixes\n- App-specific documentation\n- App-specific dependencies\n\n## 🧩 Edge Cases and Examples\n\n### **Case 1: Shared Library + App Integration**\n**Scenario**: Adding a new function to &#96;libs/p5-utils&#96; and updating &#96;duo-chrome&#96; to use it\n\n**Decision**: \n- **Primary**: 📝 Monorepo Changelog (shared library impact)\n- **Optional**: 📱 App Changelog (significant app behavior change)\n\n**Example**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nfeat(libs/p5-utils): add pressure-sensitive drawing function\n\n- Add new pressureDraw() utility for touch/stylus input\n- Update duo-chrome integration to support pressure sensitivity\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### **Case 2: Breaking Change Across Apps**\n**Scenario**: Updating shared color palette API that affects multiple apps\n\n**Decision**: 📝 Monorepo Changelog (cross-app breaking change)\n\n**Example**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nfeat(libs/color-palettes)!: update palette API for consistency\n\nBREAKING CHANGE: getPalette() now returns objects instead of arrays\n- Updated duo-chrome, crude-collage, and computational-collage to use new API\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### **Case 3: App-Specific Documentation**\n**Scenario**: Updating &#96;apps/duo-chrome/docs/user-guide.md&#96;\n\n**Decision**: 📱 App Changelog (app-specific documentation)\n\n**Example**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ndocs(duo-chrome): update user guide with new keyboard shortcuts\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### **Case 4: Cross-App Documentation**\n**Scenario**: Updating &#96;docs/architecture/overview.md&#96;\n\n**Decision**: 📝 Monorepo Changelog (workspace documentation)\n\n**Example**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ndocs(monorepo): update architecture overview with new shared components\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 🏷️ Keyword-Based Auto-Detection\n\nThe workspace changelog aggregator automatically detects entries containing these keywords:\n\n### Infrastructure Keywords\n- &#96;nx.json&#96;, &#96;nx&#96;, &#96;monorepo&#96;, &#96;workspace&#96;\n- &#96;libs/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96;, &#96;docs/&#96;\n- &#96;build&#96;, &#96;ci&#96;, &#96;deploy&#96;, &#96;release&#96;, &#96;version&#96;\n- &#96;chore(release)&#96;\n\n### When Keywords Conflict\nIf your commit message contains infrastructure keywords but the change is app-specific:\n\n**Good**: Use clear scoping\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nfeat(duo-chrome): add build optimization for this app specifically\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Avoid**: Ambiguous scoping that might trigger auto-aggregation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nfeat: optimize build process\n# ^ This might be auto-aggregated to monorepo changelog\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 🔧 Manual Override Process\n\nWhen the automatic classification doesn't match your intent:\n\n1. **After committing**: Manually edit the appropriate changelog\n2. **Re-run aggregator**: &#96;pnpm gen:changelog:apply&#96; to update workspace changelog\n3. **Document reason**: Add a note in the changelog explaining the override\n\n## 🚨 Common Mistakes to Avoid\n\n| ❌ Don't Do This | ✅ Do This Instead | Why |\n|------------------|-------------------|-----|\n| &#96;feat: add new feature&#96; | &#96;feat(duo-chrome): add color cycling&#96; | Scope indicates routing |\n| &#96;fix(monorepo): fix duo-chrome bug&#96; | &#96;fix(duo-chrome): resolve color issue&#96; | Bug is app-specific |\n| &#96;docs: update readme&#96; | &#96;docs(duo-chrome): update app readme&#96; | Specify which readme |\n| Multiple changes in one commit | Separate commits by changelog type | Easier to route correctly |\n\n## 📊 Decision Statistics\n\nUse this checklist to validate your decision:\n\n- [ ] **File paths reviewed**: What files are being modified?\n- [ ] **Impact scope assessed**: One app or multiple/shared?\n- [ ] **Change type identified**: Feature, fix, docs, refactor, etc.\n- [ ] **Keywords considered**: Does the commit message contain routing keywords?\n- [ ] **Future developers**: Will they look in the right changelog?\n\n---\n\n## 📞 When in Doubt\n\nIf you're still unsure after going through this matrix:\n\n1. **Ask the team**: Post in development chat with your scenario\n2. **Default to app-specific**: If truly uncertain, err toward app changelog\n3. **Document the decision**: Add a note explaining your reasoning\n4. **Update this matrix**: If you discover a new edge case, add it here\n\nRemember: The goal is **developer productivity** and **clear communication** - when in doubt, choose the location where future developers will most likely look for information about your change.",

```json
{

  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/michaelpaulukonis/projects/genart-monorepo/scripts/validate-changelog.js)",

  "content": "",
```
```json
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * Changelog Validation Tool\n * \n * Validates commit messages and changelog entries according to the GenArt\n * monorepo hybrid changelog classification system.\n * \n * Usage:\n *   node scripts/validate-changelog.js [options]\n *   \n * Options:\n *   --commit-msg &lt;message&gt;  Validate a specific commit message\n *   --staged               Validate staged changes\n *   --check-changelogs     Validate changelog file formats\n *   --all                  Run all validations\n */\n\nconst fs = require('fs')\nconst path = require('path')\nconst { execSync } = require('child_process')\n\n// Configuration based on docs/changelog-classification-system.md\nconst MONOREPO_KEYWORDS = [\n  'nx.json', 'nx', 'monorepo', 'workspace', \n  'libs/', 'lib/', 'docs/', 'build', 'ci', \n  'chore(release)', 'version', 'release', 'deploy'\n]\n\nconst MONOREPO_SCOPES = [\n  'monorepo', 'workspace', 'nx', 'build', 'ci', 'deploy', 'release',\n  'libs/p5-utils', 'libs/color-palettes', 'libs/version-display', 'libs/version-utils'\n]\n\nconst APP_SCOPES = [\n  'duo-chrome', 'crude-collage-painter', 'computational-collage', \n  'dragline', 'monochromifier', 'those-shape-things'\n]\n\nconst VALID_TYPES = [\n  'feat', 'fix', 'docs', 'style', 'refactor', 'test', 'chore', 'perf'\n]\n\nclass ChangelogValidator {\n  constructor() {\n    this.errors = []\n    this.warnings = []\n  }\n\n  // Validate conventional commit format\n  validateCommitMessage(message) {\n    const conventionalCommitRegex = /^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|test|chore|perf)(\\(.+\\))?(!)?: .{1,100}$/\n    \n    if (!conventionalCommitRegex.test(message)) {\n      this.errors.push('Commit message does not follow Conventional Commits format')\n      return false\n    }\n\n    const match = message.match(/^(\\w+)(\\(([^)]+)\\))?(!)?: (.+)$/)\n    if (!match) return false\n\n    const [, type, , scope, breaking, description] = match\n\n    // Validate type\n    if (!VALID_TYPES.includes(type)) {\n      this.errors.push(&#96;Invalid commit type: ${type}. Must be one of: ${VALID_TYPES.join(', ')}&#96;)\n    }\n\n    // Validate scope routing\n    if (scope) {\n      this.validateScopeRouting(type, scope, description, breaking)\n    } else {\n      this.warnings.push('Commit message lacks scope - consider adding scope for better changelog routing')\n    }\n\n    return this.errors.length === 0\n  }\n\n  validateScopeRouting(type, scope, description, breaking) {\n    const isMonorepoScope = MONOREPO_SCOPES.some(s =&gt; scope.startsWith(s))\n    const isAppScope = APP_SCOPES.includes(scope)\n    const hasMonorepoKeywords = MONOREPO_KEYWORDS.some(keyword =&gt; \n      description.toLowerCase().includes(keyword.toLowerCase()) ||\n      scope.toLowerCase().includes(keyword.toLowerCase())\n    )\n\n    // Check for scope/keyword mismatches\n    if (isAppScope &amp;&amp; hasMonorepoKeywords) {\n      this.warnings.push(\n        &#96;App scope \"${scope}\" with infrastructure keywords detected. &#96; +\n        'Consider using monorepo scope if this affects shared infrastructure.'\n      )\n    }\n\n    if (isMonorepoScope &amp;&amp; !hasMonorepoKeywords) {\n      this.warnings.push(\n        &#96;Monorepo scope \"${scope}\" without infrastructure keywords. &#96; +\n        'Verify this change actually affects shared infrastructure.'\n      )\n    }\n\n    // Breaking changes validation\n    if (breaking &amp;&amp; !isMonorepoScope) {\n      this.warnings.push(\n        'Breaking change detected in app scope. Consider if this affects multiple apps and should use monorepo scope.'\n      )\n    }\n\n    // Unknown scope validation\n    if (!isMonorepoScope &amp;&amp; !isAppScope &amp;&amp; !scope.startsWith('libs/')) {\n      this.warnings.push(&#96;Unknown scope: ${scope}. Consider using a recognized scope for proper changelog routing.&#96;)\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Validate changelog file format\n  validateChangelogFormat(filePath) {\n    if (!fs.existsSync(filePath)) {\n      this.warnings.push(&#96;Changelog file does not exist: ${filePath}&#96;)\n      return false\n    }\n\n    const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8')\n    \n    // Check for basic structure\n    if (!content.includes('# ')) {\n      this.errors.push(&#96;Changelog missing main heading: ${filePath}&#96;)\n    }\n\n    if (!content.includes('## Unreleased') &amp;&amp; !content.includes('## [Unreleased]')) {\n      this.warnings.push(&#96;Changelog missing Unreleased section: ${filePath}&#96;)\n    }\n\n    // Check for proper Markdown formatting\n    const lines = content.split('\\n')\n    let inUnreleased = false\n    let hasContent = false\n\n    for (let i = 0; i &lt; lines.length; i++) {\n      const line = lines[i]\n      \n      if (line.match(/^##\\s+\\[?Unreleased\\]?/)) {\n        inUnreleased = true\n        continue\n      }\n      \n      if (inUnreleased &amp;&amp; line.match(/^##\\s+/)) {\n        break\n      }\n      \n      if (inUnreleased &amp;&amp; line.trim() &amp;&amp; !line.startsWith('#')) {\n        hasContent = true\n        \n        // Validate list formatting\n        if (line.startsWith('- ') || line.startsWith('* ')) {\n          // Good list format\n        } else if (line.match(/^[A-Za-z]/)) {\n          this.warnings.push(&#96;Changelog entry should use list format (- or *): \"${line.trim()}\"&#96;)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    return this.errors.length === 0\n  }\n\n  // Validate staged changes for potential routing issues\n  validateStagedChanges() {\n    try {\n      const stagedFiles = execSync('git diff --cached --name-only', { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim().split('\\n').filter(Boolean)\n      \n      if (stagedFiles.length === 0) {\n        this.warnings.push('No staged changes to validate')\n        return true\n      }\n\n      // Analyze staged files for routing hints\n      const hasMonorepoFiles = stagedFiles.some(file =&gt; \n        file.startsWith('libs/') || \n        file === 'nx.json' || \n        file === 'package.json' ||\n        file.startsWith('docs/') ||\n        file.startsWith('tools/') ||\n        file.startsWith('scripts/')\n      )\n\n      const hasAppFiles = stagedFiles.some(file =&gt;   "content": "&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n# Version Management and Deployment Quick Reference\n\nThis is a quick reference for versioning and deploying apps in the GenArt monorepo.\n\n## Quick Commands\n\n### Release and Deploy (One Command)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Release and deploy a specific app (recommended)\nnx run duo-chrome:release-deploy\nnx run crude-collage-painter:release-deploy\nnx run those-shape-things:release-deploy\nnx run computational-collage:release-deploy\nnx run dragline:release-deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Separate Release and Deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Release first (using subcommands to avoid configuration conflicts)\nnx release version --projects=duo-chrome\nnx release changelog --projects=duo-chrome\n\n# Then deploy\nnx run duo-chrome:deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Multiple Apps\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Release all changed apps (version and changelog separately)\nnx release version\nnx release changelog\n\n# Deploy specific apps\nnx run duo-chrome:deploy\nnx run crude-collage-painter:deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Hybrid Changelog System\n\nThe monorepo uses a **hybrid changelog system** with two levels of changelogs:\n\n### 1. Workspace Changelog (&#96;/CHANGELOG.md&#96;)\n**Contains infrastructure and shared changes:**\n- Nx configuration updates\n- Shared library updates (&#96;libs/&#96; changes)\n- Build tool and CI improvements\n- Cross-app features\n- Monorepo-wide documentation\n\n### 2. App Changelogs (&#96;apps/[app]/CHANGELOG.md&#96;)\n**Contains app-specific changes:**\n- New features for individual apps\n- App-specific bug fixes\n- UI/UX improvements\n- App documentation updates\n\n### Automatic Routing\n\nChanges are automatically routed to the appropriate changelog based on commit message **scope**:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# → Workspace changelog (monorepo scope)\ngit commit -m \"feat(monorepo): implement hybrid changelog system\"\ngit commit -m \"feat(libs/p5-utils): add new drawing utilities\"\ngit commit -m \"chore(nx): update release configuration\"\n\n# → App changelog (app scope)\ngit commit -m \"feat(duo-chrome): add multiply blend mode\"\ngit commit -m \"fix(dragline): resolve canvas scaling issue\"\ngit commit -m \"docs(crude-collage): update user guide\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Changelog Validation\n\nUse the validation tool to ensure proper routing:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Validate a commit message\nnpm run validate:changelog -- --commit-msg \"feat(duo-chrome): add feature\"\n\n# Validate staged changes\nnpm run validate:changelog:staged\n\n# Validate all changelog files\nnpm run validate:changelog:all\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Post-Release Changelog Aggregation\n\nAfter releases, the workspace changelog is automatically updated:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# After any release, regenerate workspace changelog\nnpm run gen:changelog:apply\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis aggregates app-specific changes into the workspace changelog for a complete project overview.\n\n## Commit Message Format\n\nUse conventional commits to automatically determine version bumps:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Feature (minor version bump: 0.1.0 → 0.2.0)\ngit commit -m \"feat(duo-chrome): add new color palette\"\n\n# Bug fix (patch version bump: 0.1.0 → 0.1.1)\ngit commit -m \"fix(dragline): resolve canvas scaling issue\"\n\n# Chore/maintenance (patch version bump)\ngit commit -m \"chore(duo-chrome): update dependencies\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n",
```
```json
  "textEditContent": "# Version Management and Deployment Quick Reference\n\nThis is a quick reference for versioning and deploying apps in the GenArt monorepo.\n\n## Quick Commands\n\n### Release and Deploy (One Command)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Release and deploy a specific app (recommended)\nnx run duo-chrome:release-deploy\nnx run crude-collage-painter:release-deploy\nnx run those-shape-things:release-deploy\nnx run computational-collage:release-deploy\nnx run dragline:release-deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Separate Release and Deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Release first (using subcommands to avoid configuration conflicts)\nnx release version --projects=duo-chrome\nnx release changelog --projects=duo-chrome\n\n# Then deploy\nnx run duo-chrome:deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Multiple Apps\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Release all changed apps (version and changelog separately)\nnx release version\nnx release changelog\n\n# Deploy specific apps\nnx run duo-chrome:deploy\nnx run crude-collage-painter:deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Hybrid Changelog System\n\nThe monorepo uses a **hybrid changelog system** with two levels of changelogs:\n\n### 1. Workspace Changelog (&#96;/CHANGELOG.md&#96;)\n**Contains infrastructure and shared changes:**\n- Nx configuration updates\n- Shared library updates (&#96;libs/&#96; changes)\n- Build tool and CI improvements\n- Cross-app features\n- Monorepo-wide documentation\n\n### 2. App Changelogs (&#96;apps/[app]/CHANGELOG.md&#96;)\n**Contains app-specific changes:**\n- New features for individual apps\n- App-specific bug fixes\n- UI/UX improvements\n- App documentation updates\n\n### Automatic Routing\n\nChanges are automatically routed to the appropriate changelog based on commit message **scope**:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# → Workspace changelog (monorepo scope)\ngit commit -m \"feat(monorepo): implement hybrid changelog system\"\ngit commit -m \"feat(libs/p5-utils): add new drawing utilities\"\ngit commit -m \"chore(nx): update release configuration\"\n\n# → App changelog (app scope)\ngit commit -m \"feat(duo-chrome): add multiply blend mode\"\ngit commit -m \"fix(dragline): resolve canvas scaling issue\"\ngit commit -m \"docs(crude-collage): update user guide\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Changelog Validation\n\nUse the validation tool to ensure proper routing:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Validate a commit message\nnpm run validate:changelog -- --commit-msg \"feat(duo-chrome): add feature\"\n\n# Validate staged changes\nnpm run validate:changelog:staged\n\n# Validate all changelog files\nnpm run validate:changelog:all\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Post-Release Changelog Aggregation\n\nAfter releases, the workspace changelog is automatically updated:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# After any release, regenerate workspace changelog\nnpm run gen:changelog:apply\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis aggregates app-specific changes into the workspace changelog for a complete project overview.\n\n## Commit Message Format\n\nUse conventional commits to automatically determine version bumps:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Feature (minor version bump: 0.1.0 → 0.2.0)\ngit commit -m \"feat(duo-chrome): add new color palette\"\n\n# Bug fix (patch version bump: 0.1.0 → 0.1.1)\ngit commit -m \"fix(dragline): resolve canvas scaling issue\"\n\n# Chore/maintenance (patch version bump)\ngit commit -m \"chore(duo-chrome): update dependencies\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",
```

```json
  "content": "&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n## Troubleshooting Common Issues\n\n### \"No changes detected\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Check what commits exist since last release\ngit log --oneline $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD\n\n# Ensure commits follow conventional format\ngit log --oneline --grep=\"^feat\\|^fix\\|^chore\"\n\n# Validate commit messages\nnpm run validate:changelog:staged\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Changelog routing issues\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Check if commit will route to correct changelog\nnpm run validate:changelog -- --commit-msg \"feat(duo-chrome): your message\"\n\n# Validate all changelog files for format\nnpm run validate:changelog:all\n\n# Fix routing by updating commit message scope\ngit commit --amend -m \"feat(correct-scope): fixed message\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Release succeeded but deploy failed\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# The version is already tagged, just run deploy\nnx run app-name:deploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Workspace changelog out of sync\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Regenerate workspace changelog from app changelogs\nnpm run gen:changelog:apply\n\n# Check the result\ncat CHANGELOG.md\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Want to undo a release\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Delete the git tag (if not pushed yet)\ngit tag -d app-name@1.2.3\n\n# Reset the commit (if not pushed yet)\ngit reset --hard HEAD~1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n",
```

```javascript
/**
 * Duo-Chrome Interactive Controls System
 * 
 * An interactive duotone image composition tool with comprehensive user controls.
 * Allows independent control of two images (A and B) including size, color, and navigation.
 * 
 * Key Features:
 * - Active image selection (A/B) with visual feedback
 * - Individual size control with bounds enforcement (0.05x to 5.0x)
 * - Image navigation through collection with uniqueness enforcement
 * - Test feature: Enhanced blend mode support for improved color mixing
```

Let me provide a summary of what we've accomplished with the hybrid changelog system:

## ✅ Hybrid Changelog System Complete

**What we built:**
1. **Dual-level changelog system** - App changelogs (`CHANGELOG.md`) + workspace changelog (`CHANGELOG.md`)
2. **Smart routing** - Commit scopes determine which changelog gets the entry
3. **Validation tools** - `validate-changelog.js` checks commit format and routing
4. **Workspace aggregation** - `npm run gen:changelog:apply` pulls infrastructure changes into workspace changelog

**Key files created/updated:**
- `validate-changelog.js` - Validation tool with CLI interface
- `changelog-routing-decision-matrix.md` - Visual flowchart for routing decisions
- `copilot-instructions.md` - Enhanced commit workflow guidance
- Updated release documentation in `` and ``
- Simple README section explaining the system

**How it works:**
- `feat(duo-chrome): add feature` → App changelog
- `feat(libs/p5-utils): add utility` → Workspace changelog  
- `docs(monorepo): update guide` → Workspace changelog

**Commands:**
```bash
# Validate before commit
node scripts/validate-changelog.js --staged

# Release an app (generates app changelog)
nx run duo-chrome:release-deploy

# Update workspace changelog (after releases)
npm run gen:changelog:apply
```

The system is now fully functional and appropriately documented for a personal project - practical without being over-engineered. Ready to use!

Examine the test directory structure in the PolychromeText app\\n   - Document the configuration patterns and test organization\\n   - Identify reusable components and utilities\\n   - Note how canvas rendering and p5.js-specific elements are tested\\n\\n2. **Install Playwright dependencies**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Install Playwright at the monorepo root level\\n   cd /path/to/monorepo\\n   npm install --save-dev @playwright/test\\n   npx playwright install --with-deps\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n3. **Create shared Playwright configuration**:\\n   - Create a base &#96;playwright.config.ts&#96; file at the monorepo root:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // playwright.config.ts\\n   import { PlaywrightTestConfig } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   const baseConfig: PlaywrightTestConfig = {\\n     testDir: './tests',\\n     timeout: 30000,\\n     forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,\\n     retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,\\n     workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined,\\n     reporter: 'html',\\n     use: {\\n       baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',\\n       trace: 'on-first-retry',\\n       screenshot: 'only-on-failure',\\n     },\\n     projects: [\\n       {\\n         name: 'chromium',\\n         use: { browserName: 'chromium' },\\n       },\\n     ],\\n   };\\n\\n   export default baseConfig;\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n4. **Set up test directory structure**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Create test directories\\n   mkdir -p tests/e2e\\n   mkdir -p tests/utils\\n   mkdir -p tests/fixtures\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Create reusable test utilities**:\\n   - Canvas rendering verification:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/canvas-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function verifyCanvasExists(page: Page): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     await expect(canvas).toBeVisible();\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function verifyCanvasNotEmpty(page: Page): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     // Get canvas and check pixel data\\n     const nonEmptyCanvas = await page.evaluate(() =&gt; {\\n       const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas');\\n       if (!canvas) return false;\\n       \\n       const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');\\n       const data = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height).data;\\n       \\n       // Check if all pixels are transparent/empty\\n       for (let i = 3; i &lt; data.length; i += 4) {\\n         if (data[i] !== 0) return true;\\n       }\\n       return false;\\n     });\\n     \\n     expect(nonEmptyCanvas).toBeTruthy();\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Keyboard interaction helpers:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/keyboard-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function pressKeyAndWait(page: Page, key: string, waitTime = 100): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     await page.keyboard.press(key);\\n     await page.waitForTimeout(waitTime);\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function typeTextAndWait(page: Page, text: string, waitTime = 100): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     await page.keyboard.type(text);\\n     await page.waitForTimeout(waitTime);\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Mouse interaction helpers:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/mouse-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function clickCanvasAt(page: Page, x: number, y: number): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const box = await canvas.boundingBox();\\n     \\n     if (!box) throw new Error('Canvas not found');\\n     \\n     await page.mouse.click(box.x + x, box.y + y);\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function dragOnCanvas(page: Page, startX: number, startY: number, endX: number, endY: number): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const box = await canvas.boundingBox();\\n     \\n     if (!box) throw new Error('Canvas not found');\\n     \\n     await page.mouse.move(box.x + startX, box.y + startY);\\n     await page.mouse.down();\\n     await page.mouse.move(box.x + endX, box.y + endY);\\n     await page.mouse.up();\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Screenshot comparison utilities:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/screenshot-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import path from 'path';\\n\\n   export async function compareScreenshot(page: Page, screenshotName: string, threshold = 0.2): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const screenshotPath = path.join('tests', 'screenshots', 'reference', &#96;${screenshotName}.png&#96;);\\n     \\n     await expect(page.locator('canvas')).toHaveScreenshot(screenshotName + '.png', {\\n       maxDiffPixelRatio: threshold,\\n     });\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function captureCanvasScreenshot(page: Page, screenshotName: string): Promise&lt;string&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const screenshotPath = path.join('tests', 'screenshots', 'actual', &#96;${screenshotName}.png&#96;);\\n     \\n     await canvas.screenshot({ path: screenshotPath });\\n     return screenshotPath;\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n6. **Document the testing approach**:\\n   - Create a comprehensive testing guide at &#96;docs/testing/playwright-guide.md&#96;:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Playwright Testing Guide for p5.js Apps\\n\\n   This guide explains how to write and run Playwright tests for p5.js applications in the monorepo.\\n\\n   ## Getting Started\\n\\n   ### Running Tests\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Run all tests\\n   nx run-many --target=e2e --all\\n   \\n   # Run tests for a specific app\\n   nx run those-shape-things:e2e\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   ## Test Structure\\n   \\n   Tests are organized as follows:\\n   - Use the provided utilities:\\n\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import { verifyCanvasExists, verifyCanvasNotEmpty } from {\\n       console.log('No affected apps detected. Remember to commit the changes.');\\n   }\\n   \\n   // Parse command line arguments\\n   const args = process.argv.slice(2);\\n   const versionBump = args[0] || 'patch';\\n   updateVersions(versionBump);\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n3. **Integration with Build/Release Process**:\\n   - dependencies across the monorepo to establish a clean separation between workspace-level and app-specific dependencies:\\n\\n1. **Dependency Analysis**:\\n   - Create a script to analyze all package.json files in the monorepo:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   const fs = require('fs');\\n   const path = require('path');\\n   const glob = require('glob');\\n   \\n   // Read workspace root package.json\\n   const rootPkg = require('./package.json');\\n   const rootDeps = {...rootPkg.dependencies, ...rootPkg.devDependencies};\\n   \\n   // Find all app package.json files\\n   const appPackageJsons = glob.sync('./apps/*/package.json');\\n   \\n   const analysis = {\\n     duplicates: [],\\n     versionMismatches: [],\\n     appSpecific: {},\\n     unused: []\\n   };\\n   \\n   appPackageJsons.forEach(pkgPath =&gt; {\\n     const appName = path.dirname(pkgPath).split('/').pop();\\n     const appPkg = require(pkgPath);\\n     const appDeps = {...appPkg.dependencies, ...appPkg.devDependencies};\\n     \\n     analysis.appSpecific[appName] = [];\\n     \\n     // Check for duplicates and mismatches\\n     Object.entries(appDeps).forEach(([dep, version]) =&gt; {\\n       if (rootDeps[dep]) {\\n         analysis.duplicates.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         \\n         if (version !== rootDeps[dep]) {\\n           analysis.versionMismatches.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         }\\n       } else {\\n         analysis.appSpecific[appName].push({dep, version});\\n       }\\n     });\\n   });\\n   \\n   // Output analysis results\\n   console.log(JSON.stringify(analysis, null, 2));\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n2. **Dependency Categorization**:\\n   - Identify build tools that should be managed at workspace level only:\\n     - Vite, ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, Nx, Jest, Playwright, etc.\\n   - Identify runtime dependencies that should be shared:\\n     - React, p5.js, common UI libraries, utility libraries\\n   - Identify app-specific dependencies that should remain local:\\n     - Specialized libraries used by only one app\\n     - App-specific plugins or extensions\\n\\n3. **Dependency Cleanup**:\\n   - Move all build tools to workspace root package.json:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Example: moving ESLint from app to root\\n   npm uninstall eslint --workspace=app-name\\n   npm install eslint --save-dev\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Standardize versions for shared dependencies:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Update all apps to use the same version as root\\n   npm install react@workspace-version --workspace=app-name\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Remove unused dependencies identified during analysis\\n   - Keep truly app-specific dependencies in their respective package.json files\\n\\n4. **Documentation Update**:\\n   - Create a dependency management strategy document in docs/architecture/:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Dependency Management Strategy\\n   \\n   ## Workspace-level Dependencies\\n   - **Build Tools**: All build tools (Vite, ESLint, TypeScript, etc.) are managed at the workspace level\\n   - **Shared Runtime Dependencies**: Common libraries used across multiple apps\\n   \\n   ## App-level Dependencies\\n   - Only dependencies that are truly specific to a single app\\n   - Must not duplicate workspace dependencies\\n   \\n   ## Adding New Dependencies\\n   1. Determine if the dependency will be used by multiple apps\\n      - If yes: Add to workspace root\\n      - If no: Add to specific app\\n   \\n   ## Version Management\\n   - All shared dependencies must use the same version across the workspace\\n   - Version upgrades should be coordinated across all affected packages\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   \\n   - Update adding-projects.md with clear guidelines:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   ## Dependency Management\\n   \\n   When adding dependencies to your project:\\n   \\n   1. Check if the dependency already exists in the workspace root\\n      - If yes: Do not add it to your app's package.json\\n   \\n   2. For build tools (Vite, ESLint, etc.):\\n      - These should only be added to workspace root\\n      - Configure as needed in your app\\n   \\n   3. For app-specific dependencies:\\n      - Add only to your app's package.json\\n      - Document why this dependency is needed\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Testing and Verification**:\\n   - Run builds for all apps to ensure they still function correctly\\n   - ## Current Test Setup Analysis

### 1. **Nx vs Root `package.json` Paradigm**

You're right to question the root `package.json` approach. In an Nx monorepo, tests should primarily be configured at the **project level** in each app's `project.json`, not in the root `package.json`.

### 2. **Current Test Architecture**

Your monorepo has a **hybrid approach**:

**✅ Proper Nx way (project-level):**
- `duo-chrome` and `monochromifier` have `` targets in their `project.json`
- Example: `"test": { "executor": "nx:run-commands", "options": { "command": "node src/size-control.test.js" }}`

**❌ Legacy approach (root package.json):**
- App-specific tests in root: `"test:crude-collage": "cross-env TEST_APP=crude-collage-painter playwright test"`
- Global test runners: `"test": "nx run-many --target=test --all"`

### 3. **How to Use Nx for Tests**

**Individual project tests:**
```bash
# Run tests for a specific app (if it has a test target)
nx test duo-chrome
nx test monochromifier

# Run all tests across projects that have test targets
nx run-many --target=test --all
```

**E2E tests (Playwright):**
```bash
# Root-level e2e tests (testing multiple apps)
nx run test:e2e

# App-specific e2e tests
nx test:e2e crude-collage-painter
```

## Recommended Migration Strategy

### 1. **Add test targets to missing apps**

Apps like `crude-collage-painter`, `computational-collage`, etc. should have test targets in their `project.json`:

```json
{
  "targets": {
    "test": {
      "executor": "@nx/playwright:playwright",
      "options": {
        "config": "apps/crude-collage-painter/playwright.config.js"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 2. **Clean up root `package.json`**

Remove app-specific test scripts and keep only:
- `"test": "nx run-many --target=test --all"` (runs all project tests)
- `"test:e2e": "playwright test"` (global e2e tests)

### 3. **Nx Advantages for Testing**

- **Caching**: Nx caches test results and only reruns changed tests
- **Dependency awareness**: Tests run in dependency order
- **Parallel execution**: Multiple test suites can run simultaneously
- **Affected testing**: `nx affected:test` only tests changed projects

## Next Steps

Would you like me to:

1. **Migrate the test configuration** by adding proper test targets to the apps that don't have them?
2. **Clean up the root `package.json`** to follow Nx best practices?
3. **Set up a unified testing strategy** across all apps?

The key insight is that Nx monorepos work best when each project (app/lib) owns its testing configuration, rather than centralizing everything in the root package.json.

Examine the test directory structure in the PolychromeText app\\n   - Document the configuration patterns and test organization\\n   - Identify reusable components and utilities\\n   - Note how canvas rendering and p5.js-specific elements are tested\\n\\n2. **Install Playwright dependencies**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Install Playwright at the monorepo root level\\n   cd /path/to/monorepo\\n   npm install --save-dev @playwright/test\\n   npx playwright install --with-deps\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n3. **Create shared Playwright configuration**:\\n   - Create a base &#96;playwright.config.ts&#96; file at the monorepo root:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // playwright.config.ts\\n   import { PlaywrightTestConfig } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   const baseConfig: PlaywrightTestConfig = {\\n     testDir: './tests',\\n     timeout: 30000,\\n     forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,\\n     retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 0,\\n     workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined,\\n     reporter: 'html',\\n     use: {\\n       baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',\\n       trace: 'on-first-retry',\\n       screenshot: 'only-on-failure',\\n     },\\n     projects: [\\n       {\\n         name: 'chromium',\\n         use: { browserName: 'chromium' },\\n       },\\n     ],\\n   };\\n\\n   export default baseConfig;\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n4. **Set up test directory structure**:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Create test directories\\n   mkdir -p tests/e2e\\n   mkdir -p tests/utils\\n   mkdir -p tests/fixtures\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Create reusable test utilities**:\\n   - Canvas rendering verification:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/canvas-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function verifyCanvasExists(page: Page): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     await expect(canvas).toBeVisible();\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function verifyCanvasNotEmpty(page: Page): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     // Get canvas and check pixel data\\n     const nonEmptyCanvas = await page.evaluate(() =&gt; {\\n       const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas');\\n       if (!canvas) return false;\\n       \\n       const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');\\n       const data = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height).data;\\n       \\n       // Check if all pixels are transparent/empty\\n       for (let i = 3; i &lt; data.length; i += 4) {\\n         if (data[i] !== 0) return true;\\n       }\\n       return false;\\n     });\\n     \\n     expect(nonEmptyCanvas).toBeTruthy();\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Keyboard interaction helpers:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/keyboard-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function pressKeyAndWait(page: Page, key: string, waitTime = 100): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     await page.keyboard.press(key);\\n     await page.waitForTimeout(waitTime);\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function typeTextAndWait(page: Page, text: string, waitTime = 100): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     await page.keyboard.type(text);\\n     await page.waitForTimeout(waitTime);\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Mouse interaction helpers:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/mouse-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page } from '@playwright/test';\\n\\n   export async function clickCanvasAt(page: Page, x: number, y: number): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const box = await canvas.boundingBox();\\n     \\n     if (!box) throw new Error('Canvas not found');\\n     \\n     await page.mouse.click(box.x + x, box.y + y);\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function dragOnCanvas(page: Page, startX: number, startY: number, endX: number, endY: number): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const box = await canvas.boundingBox();\\n     \\n     if (!box) throw new Error('Canvas not found');\\n     \\n     await page.mouse.move(box.x + startX, box.y + startY);\\n     await page.mouse.down();\\n     await page.mouse.move(box.x + endX, box.y + endY);\\n     await page.mouse.up();\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   - Screenshot comparison utilities:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   // tests/utils/screenshot-helpers.ts\\n   import { Page, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import path from 'path';\\n\\n   export async function compareScreenshot(page: Page, screenshotName: string, threshold = 0.2): Promise&lt;void&gt; {\\n     const screenshotPath = path.join('tests', 'screenshots', 'reference', &#96;${screenshotName}.png&#96;);\\n     \\n     await expect(page.locator('canvas')).toHaveScreenshot(screenshotName + '.png', {\\n       maxDiffPixelRatio: threshold,\\n     });\\n   }\\n\\n   export async function captureCanvasScreenshot(page: Page, screenshotName: string): Promise&lt;string&gt; {\\n     const canvas = page.locator('canvas');\\n     const screenshotPath = path.join('tests', 'screenshots', 'actual', &#96;${screenshotName}.png&#96;);\\n     \\n     await canvas.screenshot({ path: screenshotPath });\\n     return screenshotPath;\\n   }\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n6. **Document the testing approach**:\\n   - Create a comprehensive testing guide at &#96;docs/testing/playwright-guide.md&#96;:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Playwright Testing Guide for p5.js Apps\\n\\n   This guide explains how to write and run Playwright tests for p5.js applications in the monorepo.\\n\\n   ## Getting Started\\n\\n   ### Running Tests\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Run all tests\\n   nx run-many --target=e2e --all\\n   \\n   # Run tests for a specific app\\n   nx run those-shape-things:e2e\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   ## Test Structure\\n   \\n   Tests are organized as follows:\\n   - &#96;tests/e2e/&#96;: End-to-end tests for applications\\n   - &#96;tests/utils/&#96;: Shared test utilities\\n   - &#96;tests/fixtures/&#96;: Test data and fixtures\\n\\n   ## Writing Tests for p5.js Apps\\n\\n   ### Canvas Testing\\n   \\n   Canvas elements require special handling. Use the provided utilities:\\n\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import { verifyCanvasExists, verifyCanvasNotEmpty } from '../../utils/canvas-helpers';\\n\\n   test('should render canvas with content', async ({ page }) =&gt; {\\n     await page.goto('/apps/my-app/');\\n     await verifyCanvasExists(page);\\n     await verifyCanvasNotEmpty(page);\\n   });\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   ### Testing User Interactions\\n   \\n   For testing keyboard and mouse interactions:\\n\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   import { respond to user input', async ({ page }) =&gt; {\\n     await page.goto('/apps/my-app/');\\n     \\n     // Test keyboard interaction\\n     await pressKeyAndWait(page, 'b');\\n     \\n     // Test mouse interaction\\n     await clickCanvasAt(page, 100, 100);\\n     \\n     // Verify expected changes\\n     // ...\\n   });\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n   ### Visual Regression Testing\\n   \\n   For comparing canvas output against reference images:\\n\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\n   import { test } from '@playwright/test';\\n   import { compareScreenshot } from page }) =&gt; {\\n     // Get initial background color\\n     const initialBgColor = await page.evaluate(() =&gt; {\\n       return \"Review all app package.json files against workspace root package.json to identify and resolve duplications, version mismatches, and optimize dependency management across the monorepo.\",\n        \"status\": \"pending\",\n        \"priority\": \"medium\",\n        \"dependencies\": [\n          \"30\"\n        ],\n        \"details\": \"This task involves conducting a comprehensive audit of dependencies across the monorepo to establish a clean separation between workspace-level and app-specific dependencies:\\n\\n1. **Dependency Analysis**:\\n   - Create a script to analyze all package.json files in the monorepo:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   const fs = require('fs');\\n   const path = require('path');\\n   const glob = require('glob');\\n   \\n   // Read workspace root package.json\\n   const rootPkg = require('./package.json');\\n   const rootDeps = {...rootPkg.dependencies, ...rootPkg.devDependencies};\\n   \\n   // Find all app package.json files\\n   const appPackageJsons = glob.sync('./apps/*/package.json');\\n   \\n   const analysis = {\\n     duplicates: [],\\n     versionMismatches: [],\\n     appSpecific: {},\\n     unused: []\\n   };\\n   \\n   appPackageJsons.forEach(pkgPath =&gt; {\\n     const appName = path.dirname(pkgPath).split('/').pop();\\n     const appPkg = require(pkgPath);\\n     const appDeps = {...appPkg.dependencies, ...appPkg.devDependencies};\\n     \\n     analysis.appSpecific[appName] = [];\\n     \\n     // Check for duplicates and mismatches\\n     Object.entries(appDeps).forEach(([dep, version]) =&gt; {\\n       if (rootDeps[dep]) {\\n         analysis.duplicates.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         \\n         if (version !== rootDeps[dep]) {\\n           analysis.versionMismatches.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         }\\n       } else {\\n         analysis.appSpecific[appName].push({dep, version});\\n       }\\n     });\\n   });\\n   \\n   // Output analysis results\\n   console.log(JSON.stringify(analysis, null, 2));\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n2. **Dependency Categorization**:\\n   - Identify build tools that should be managed at workspace level only:\\n     - Vite, ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, Nx, Jest, Playwright, etc.\\n   - Identify runtime dependencies that should be shared:\\n     - React, p5.js, common UI libraries, utility libraries\\n   - Identify app-specific dependencies that should remain local:\\n     - Specialized libraries used by only one app\\n     - App-specific plugins or extensions\\n\\n3. **Dependency Cleanup**:\\n   - Move all build tools to workspace root package.json:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Example: moving ESLint from app to root\\n   npm {
```json
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/michaelpaulukonis/projects/genart-monorepo/docs/plans/02.nx-testing-migration-strategy.md)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/michaelpaulukonis/projects/genart-monorepo/docs/plans/02.nx-testing-migration-strategy.md)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "# 02. Nx Testing Migration Strategy\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe GenArt monorepo currently uses a hybrid testing approach that mixes proper Nx project-level test targets with legacy root-level package.json scripts. This creates inconsistency in how tests are configured and executed across applications, deviates from Nx best practices, and makes it difficult to scale testing as the monorepo grows.\n\n### Current Issues\n- **Inconsistent Test Configuration**: Only 2 out of 6 apps (duo-chrome, monochromifier) have proper &#96;test&#96; targets in their &#96;project.json&#96; files\n- **Legacy Root Scripts**: App-specific test scripts like &#96;test:crude-collage&#96;, &#96;test:computational-collage&#96; exist in root &#96;package.json&#96; instead of proper Nx targets\n- **Missing Nx Integration**: Apps without test targets cannot be tested using standard Nx commands (&#96;nx test app-name&#96;)\n- **Scaling Challenges**: Adding new apps requires manual updates to root package.json rather than self-contained configuration\n\n### Current State Analysis\n**✅ Strengths (already implemented):**\n- Comprehensive Playwright testing infrastructure (Task 17 completed)\n- Excellent test utilities adapted from PolychromeText in &#96;test/utils/p5-canvas-helpers.js&#96;\n- Thorough documentation in &#96;docs/testing/&#96;\n- Working e2e tests for duo-chrome and monorepo integration\n- Multi-app testing support via &#96;TEST_APP&#96; environment variable\n\n**❌ Gaps requiring migration:**\n- Missing test targets: crude-collage-painter, computational-collage, those-shape-things, dragline\n- App-specific scripts in root package.json instead of project-level configuration\n- No standardized test patterns across all apps\n\n## Requirements\n\n### R1: Nx-First Test Configuration\n**Requirement**: All applications must have proper test targets in their &#96;project.json&#96; files that can be executed via &#96;nx test app-name&#96;\n\n**Acceptance Criteria**:\n- Each app has a &#96;test&#96; target using &#96;@nx/playwright:playwright&#96; executor\n- All existing test functionality is preserved during migration\n- Global test execution via &#96;nx run-many --target=test --all&#96; works correctly\n- Individual app testing via &#96;nx test app-name&#96; works for all apps\n\n### R2: Root Package.json Cleanup\n**Requirement**: Remove app-specific test scripts from root package.json and retain only workspace-level commands\n\n**Acceptance Criteria**:\n- App-specific scripts (&#96;test:crude-collage&#96;, &#96;test:computational-collage&#96;) are removed\n- Only workspace-level scripts remain: &#96;test&#96;, &#96;test:e2e&#96;, &#96;test:e2e:ui&#96;, etc.\n- All existing test functionality remains accessible through Nx commands\n- No breaking changes to CI/CD pipelines or developer workflows\n\n### R3: Standardized Test Infrastructure\n**Requirement**: Establish consistent test patterns and configuration across all applications\n\n**Acceptance Criteria**:\n- All apps use the same Playwright configuration patterns\n- Shared test utilities work across all applications\n- Each app has a basic smoke test to verify Playwright integration\n- Documentation is updated to reflect the new Nx-first approach\n\n### R4: Backward Compatibility\n**Requirement**: Maintain all existing test functionality throughout the migration\n\n**Acceptance Criteria**:\n- No test capabilities are lost during migration\n- All existing test files continue to work\n- Performance characteristics are maintained or improved\n- Existing CI/CD integration continues to function\n\n## Technical Approach\n\n### Architecture Overview\nThe migration follows Nx monorepo best practices by moving test configuration from the workspace root to individual project configurations. This approach provides:\n\n- **Encapsulation**: Each app owns its test configuration\n- **Scalability**: New apps are self-contained without requiring workspace updates\n- **Consistency**: All apps follow the same configuration patterns\n- **Maintainability**: Test configuration is co-located with app code\n\n### Configuration Strategy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Target configuration for each app's project.json\n{\n  \"test\": {\n    \"executor\": \"@nx/playwright:playwright\",\n    \"options\": {\n      \"config\": \"apps/{app-name}/playwright.config.js\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Shared Infrastructure Reuse\nThe migration leverages existing infrastructure:\n- Playwright configuration base from root &#96;playwright.config.js&#96;\n- Test utilities in &#96;test/utils/p5-canvas-helpers.js&#96;\n- Documentation patterns from &#96;docs/testing/&#96;\n- Multi-app support via &#96;TEST_APP&#96; environment variable\n\n## Implementation Steps\n\n### Phase 1: Project Configuration Migration (High Priority)\n1. **Audit Current Test Targets**\n   - Document which apps have test targets and which don't\n   - Identify configuration patterns from existing targets (duo-chrome, monochromifier)\n   - Map current root package.json scripts to target apps\n\n2. **Create Missing Test Targets**\n   - Add test targets to crude-collage-painter project.json\n   - Add test targets to computational-collage project.json\n   - Add test targets to those-shape-things project.json\n   - Add test targets to dragline project.json\n\n3. **Create App-Specific Playwright Configs**\n   - Create playwright.config.js for each app that needs one\n   - Base configurations on existing root config with app-specific overrides\n   - Ensure TEST_APP environment variable compatibility\n\n4. **Validation Testing**\n   - Test each app's test target individually (&#96;nx test app-name&#96;)\n   - Verify all existing test functionality works\n   - Test global command (&#96;nx run-many --target=test --all&#96;)\n\n### Phase 2: Root Package.json Cleanup (High Priority)\n5. **Remove Legacy Scripts**\n   - Remove &#96;test:crude-collage&#96; and &#96;test:computational-collage&#96; scripts\n   - Update any documentation referencing the removed scripts\n   - Verify no CI/CD dependencies on removed scripts\n\n6. **Standardize Workspace Scripts**\n   - Keep &#96;test&#96;: &#96;nx run-many --target=test --all&#96;\n   - Keep e2e scripts for global testing\n   - Document the final script structure\n\n### Phase 3: Standardization and Documentation (Medium Priority)\n7. **Create Standard Test Templates**\n   - Develop smoke test templates for apps without comprehensive tests\n   - Ensure all apps have basic Playwright integration tests\n   - Validate test utilities work across all app types\n\n8. **Update Documentation**\n   - Update docs/testing/ to reflect Nx-first approach\n   - Update docs/guides/adding-projects.md with test target requirements\n   - Create migration guide for existing developers\n\n9. **Cross-App Validation**\n   - Test the multi-app TEST_APP approach across all applications\n   - Verify shared test utilities work with all p5.js instance mode implementations\n   - Performance test the global test suite\n\n### Phase 4: Advanced Features (Low Priority)\n10. **Performance Optimization**\n    - Implement parallel testing where beneficial\n    - Optimize test execution for CI environments\n    - Add caching strategies for test results\n\n11. **Enhanced Test Coverage**\n    - Expand test suites for apps with minimal coverage\n    - Add visual regression testing for all apps\n    - Implement cross-browser testing where needed\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Migration Validation\nEach phase includes comprehensive validation:\n\n**Phase 1 Validation**:\n- Individual app tests: &#96;nx test duo-chrome&#96;, &#96;nx test crude-collage-painter&#96;, etc.\n- Global test execution: &#96;nx run-many --target=test --all&#96;\n- Comparison with pre-migration test results\n- Performance benchmarking\n\n**Phase 2 Validation**:\n- Verify removed scripts no longer exist\n- Test alternative commands work: &#96;nx test&#96; instead of &#96;npm run test:crude-collage&#96;\n- CI/CD pipeline testing if applicable\n\n**Phase 3 Validation**:\n- Cross-app compatibility testing\n- Documentation review and validation\n- Test template functionality\n\n### Regression Testing\n- Compare test execution times before/after migration\n- Verify all existing test files continue to pass\n- Validate TEST_APP environment variable functionality\n- Cross-browser testing on key applications\n\n### Quality Gates\nEach implementation step must pass:\n1. **Functional Tests**: All existing tests continue to pass\n2. **Configuration Tests**: Nx commands work as expected\n3. **Performance Tests**: No significant performance degradation\n4. **Integration Tests**: Global test commands work correctly\n\n## Risks &amp; Mitigation\n\n### Risk 1: Test Configuration Conflicts\n**Risk**: App-specific Playwright configs might conflict with shared utilities\n**Probability**: Medium  \n**Impact**: Medium  \n**Mitigation**: \n- Use consistent base configuration across all apps\n- Test configurations incrementally during Phase 1\n- Maintain fallback to root configuration if needed\n\n### Risk 2: CI/CD Pipeline Disruption\n**Risk**: Changes to test scripts might break automated pipelines\n**Probability**: Low  \n**Impact**: High  \n**Mitigation**:\n- Audit CI/CD dependencies before making changes\n- Implement migration during low-activity periods\n- Maintain backward compatibility during transition\n\n### Risk 3: Developer Workflow Disruption\n**Risk**: Developers accustomed to legacy commands might be confused\n**Probability**: Medium  \n**Impact**: Low  \n**Mitigation**:\n- Create comprehensive migration documentation\n- Provide command mapping (old → new)\n- Implement gradual rollout with team communication\n\n### Risk 4: Test Utility Compatibility\n**Risk**: Shared test utilities might not work correctly across all app types\n**Probability**: Low  \n**Impact**: Medium  \n**Mitigation**:\n- Comprehensive cross-app testing in Phase 3\n- Adapt utilities if needed for specific app requirements\n- Maintain app-specific overrides where necessary\n\n## Dependencies\n\n### Internal Dependencies\n- **Task 17**: Playwright infrastructure (✅ Completed) - Required foundation\n- **Current Apps**: All 6 applications must be stable for migration testing\n- **Nx Configuration**: Proper Nx workspace setup (✅ Available)\n\n### External Dependencies\n- **@nx/playwright**: Nx Playwright plugin (✅ Installed)\n- **Playwright**:     \"title\": \"Audit and Optimize Package Dependencies Across Workspace\",\n        \"description\": \"Review all app package.json files against workspace root package.json to identify and resolve duplications, version mismatches, and optimize dependency management across the monorepo.\",\n        \"status\": \"pending\",\n        \"priority\": \"medium\",\n        \"dependencies\": [\n          \"30\"\n        ],\n        \"details\": \"This task involves conducting a comprehensive audit of dependencies across the monorepo to establish a clean separation between workspace-level and app-specific dependencies:\\n\\n1. **Dependency Analysis**:\\n   - Create a script to analyze all package.json files in the monorepo:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\\n   const fs = require('fs');\\n   const path = require('path');\\n   const glob = require('glob');\\n   \\n   // Read workspace root package.json\\n   const rootPkg = require('./package.json');\\n   const rootDeps = {...rootPkg.dependencies, ...rootPkg.devDependencies};\\n   \\n   // Find all app package.json files\\n   const appPackageJsons = glob.sync('./apps/*/package.json');\\n   \\n   const analysis = {\\n     duplicates: [],\\n     versionMismatches: [],\\n     appSpecific: {},\\n     unused: []\\n   };\\n   \\n   appPackageJsons.forEach(pkgPath =&gt; {\\n     const appName = path.dirname(pkgPath).split('/').pop();\\n     const appPkg = require(pkgPath);\\n     const appDeps = {...appPkg.dependencies, ...appPkg.devDependencies};\\n     \\n     analysis.appSpecific[appName] = [];\\n     \\n     // Check for duplicates and mismatches\\n     Object.entries(appDeps).forEach(([dep, version]) =&gt; {\\n       if (rootDeps[dep]) {\\n         analysis.duplicates.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         \\n         if (version !== rootDeps[dep]) {\\n           analysis.versionMismatches.push({app: appName, dep, appVersion: version, rootVersion: rootDeps[dep]});\\n         }\\n       } else {\\n         analysis.appSpecific[appName].push({dep, version});\\n       }\\n     });\\n   });\\n   \\n   // Output analysis results\\n   console.log(JSON.stringify(analysis, null, 2));\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n2. **Dependency Categorization**:\\n   - Identify build tools that should be managed at workspace level only:\\n     - Vite, ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, Nx, Jest, Playwright, etc.\\n   - Identify runtime dependencies that should be shared:\\n     - React, p5.js, common UI libraries, utility libraries\\n   - Identify app-specific dependencies that should remain local:\\n     - Specialized libraries used by only one app\\n     - App-specific plugins or extensions\\n\\n3. **Dependency Cleanup**:\\n   - Move all build tools to workspace root package.json:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Example: moving ESLint from app to root\\n   npm uninstall eslint --workspace=app-name\\n   npm install eslint --save-dev\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Standardize versions for shared dependencies:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\n   # Update all apps to use the same version as root\\n   npm install react@workspace-version --workspace=app-name\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   - Remove unused dependencies identified during analysis\\n   - Keep truly app-specific dependencies in their respective package.json files\\n\\n4. **Documentation Update**:\\n   - Create a dependency management strategy document in docs/architecture/:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   # Dependency Management Strategy\\n   \\n   ## Workspace-level Dependencies\\n   - **Build Tools**: All build tools (Vite, ESLint, TypeScript, etc.) are managed at the workspace level\\n   - **Shared Runtime Dependencies**: Common libraries used across multiple apps\\n   \\n   ## App-level Dependencies\\n   - Only dependencies that are truly specific to a single app\\n   - Must not duplicate workspace dependencies\\n   \\n   ## Adding New Dependencies\\n   1. Determine if the dependency will be used by multiple apps\\n      - If yes: Add to workspace root\\n      - If no: Add to specific app\\n   \\n   ## Version Management\\n   - All shared dependencies must use the same version across the workspace\\n   - Version upgrades should be coordinated across all affected packages\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n   \\n   - Update adding-projects.md with clear guidelines:\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\\n   ## Dependency Management\\n   \\n   When adding dependencies to your project:\\n   \\n   1. Check if the dependency already exists in the workspace root\\n      - If yes: Do not add it to your app's package.json\\n   \\n   2. For build tools (Vite, ESLint, etc.):\\n      - These should only be added to workspace root\\n      - Configure as needed in your app\\n   \\n   3. For app-specific dependencies:\\n      - Add only to your app's package.json\\n      - Document why this dependency is needed\\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\\n\\n5. **Testing and Verification**:\\n   - Run builds for all apps to ensure they still function correctly\\n   -
```
